# ROADMAP - `andes-sim`: a multi-engine simulation framework

> Scope of this file: building the `andes-sim` C++ framework. It supersedes the
> earlier "rewrite hsim (CoSIM-ready)" content in this file. It does NOT replace
> the repo-root `ROADMAP.md` (the master FR tracker). One feature per session;
> update each feature's **State** as you go.

## Goal

Turn the Python `hsim` driver into a single compiled C++20 executable named
**`andes-sim`** that is a *framework* hosting multiple simulator backends behind
one clear, self-describing interface - so QEMU (fast), Verilator (accurate),
Hybrid, and future simulators (alioth, sid) are all first-class, and new
Verilator builds can be added at runtime with no framework rebuild.

## Vocabulary (three orthogonal concepts)

- **Engine** = one simulator *process* the framework drives: `qemu`,
  `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`, `verilator:ax66_makatau`, later `alioth`, `sid`.
  This is the *pluggable* unit. Verilator has many engine instances (one per HW
  config); QEMU has one.
- **Model** = how chosen engines compose for a run:
  - `fast`     = QEMU alone (functional).
  - `accurate` = one Verilator alone, **pure - from reset, no QEMU** (cycle-accurate).
  - `hybrid`   = QEMU fast-forward -> Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
- **Trigger** = the ROI delimiter, used by `hybrid`: `csr` | `pc` | `icount` | `simpoint`.

A run is `(model) x (engine) x (trigger)`.

## Locked decisions

- **Name:** the binary is `andes-sim` (the `hsim` "hybrid-sim" name retires).
- **Language: C++20**, existing clang++ toolchain; `#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"`
  directly (no hand-copied struct, no offsets).
- **Runtime = pure C++** (no Python, no shell on the run path). **Build and test
  infrastructure may stay shell/Python.**
- **Plugins are drop-in binaries, not linked libraries.** Engines are external
  processes; `andes-sim` is never recompiled to add one. No `dlopen`, no
  compiled-in engine list.
- **Discovery = scan + `--describe`.** The framework scans an engines directory
  and asks each binary to self-report its capabilities as JSON. A sidecar
  `<bin>.json` is the fallback for binaries that cannot add the flag. This is the
  hot-plug query mechanism.
- **Transparent passthrough for `fast`/`accurate`.** The framework parses only its
  selection flags; everything after `--` forwards verbatim to the engine. In these
  modes it inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, applies **no timeout**, and propagates the
  engine's exit code (exec-style). All native engine behavior is preserved - e.g.
  QEMU can hold a gdbstub and wait for a debugger. Users experience one simulator.
- **`accurate` = pure Verilator from reset, no QEMU.** vsim already supports this
  (default path; hybrid is gated by `--resume-from-qemu`). Cycles come from vsim's
  own output, not a drained state file.
- **No QEMU2 handback.** No gdbstub state-restore into a second QEMU. The `hybrid`
  cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta. The QEMU2 leg was removed from the repo
  entirely (`tests/e2e.sh` is a 2-phase harness now); see `remove_qemu2.md`.
- **No CoSIM.** Dropped from this design.

## Architecture (three layers)

```
 andes-sim  (one C++20 binary; libc++ + include/hybrid/state_abi.h only)
   |
 [1] ENGINE REGISTRY  -- discover at runtime (the hot-plug seam)
   |     scan engines dir -> run `<bin> --describe` -> EngineDescriptor (JSON)
   |     qemu (built-in descriptor) | verilator:<cfg> (self-describe) | alioth/sid (self-describe)
   |
 [2] MODEL = composition  -- how chosen engines combine
   |     fast      = [ qemu ]                      transparent passthrough
   |     accurate  = [ verilator:<cfg> ]           transparent passthrough (from reset)
   |     hybrid    = [ qemu --ff--> verilator ]    orchestrated, + trigger
   |
 [3] PLAN EXECUTOR  -- (hybrid only) spawn legs, thread hybrid_state_v1, read mcycle
         run_plan(steps): per step -> registry invoke template -> spawn+timeout -> drain
```

`fast`/`accurate` bypass layer [3] entirely (exec-passthrough). Only `hybrid`
orchestrates.

## Engine interface (the contract alioth/sid follow)

A simulator joins the framework by doing two things:

**1. Self-describe.** Answer `--describe` with one JSON object:

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",            // qemu | verilator | alioth | sid | ...
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",       // functional | cycle-accurate
  "vlen":     512, "xlen": 64,        // optional HW params
  "triggers": ["csr","pc","icount"],  // ROI delimiters understood
  "roles":    ["standalone","accurate-leg"],  // standalone | fast-leg | accurate-leg
  "state":    ["resume","drain"],     // hybrid_state_v1 capabilities (omit if none)
  "invoke": {                         // argv prefix per role; {placeholders} filled by the framework
     "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
     "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                      "--handoff-out", "{state_out}", "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"         // where the measurement is: stderr:<re> | state.mcycle
}
```

**2. Speak the ABI for any role it claims.** Any engine listing `resume`/`drain`
in `state` must read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte
(`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) and honor the shared-mmap convention. A
functional-only engine (`fast-leg`/`standalone`, no `state`) needs none of this.

The framework needs **zero per-engine code** - everything it must know comes back
from `--describe`. Spec lives in `docs/engine_interface.md` (delivered in F2).

## Conventions

- **TDD.** Each feature: failing test first (RED), smallest code to pass (GREEN),
  refactor. Run all fast tests each time.
- **Parity flywheel for carried-over behavior.** `tests/andes_sim/parity.sh` runs
  the same args through `python3 hsim.py` (golden) and `build/andes-sim` and diffs
  stdout/stderr/rc. Parity covers behavior that survives unchanged: `list
  fixtures`, `doctor`, `build --dry-run`, `hybrid` cycle figures, `profile`/
  `cluster`/`simpoint`/`estimate`, `archive`. Byte-exact where output is fixed;
  cycle-figure equivalence for hybrid/estimate.
- **New surface gets fresh acceptance tests** (no python golden exists for it):
  `--model fast|accurate`, `--` passthrough, `list engines`, self-describe.
- **Existing smoke tests** `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are binary-agnostic; reuse
  as acceptance tests, migrate names in F14.
- During development the binary is `build/andes-sim`; Python `hsim` stays at repo
  root as the golden reference until F14 swaps it.
- **State** values: `NOT STARTED` -> `IN PROGRESS` -> `DONE`.

## Reuse (do not reinvent)

- `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - read drained files into `struct hybrid_state_v1`.
- `hsim` (Python) - authoritative behavior spec for carried-over subcommands.
- `tools/orchestrator/plan.py` - Session/Step model -> the C++ phase-plan engine.
- `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` - argv builders (QEMU drain, vsim) minus QEMU2.
- `tools/hsim_shm.py` - `parse_size`/`select_mmap_dir`/`allocate` (port).
- `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py::write_archive` + `_build_meta` (port).
- `tests/lib/roi.sh` + `tests/e2e.sh` PC resolution - port symbol lookup by reading
  the ELF `.symtab` in C++.
- vsim arg surface `verilator/src/main.cpp:189-304` (optparse) - where `--describe`
  is added; `--print-config:197-200` is the model to copy; `NDS_VLEN` is the source.

---

## Features

### F0 - Scaffold, build, parity harness
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** Standalone C++20 project that compiles `andes-sim` with a
  subcommand-dispatch skeleton and REPO_ROOT discovery (`/proc/self/exe` ->
  `readlink`). Bootstrap build script and the differential parity harness later
  features lean on.
- **Key files:** `driver/CMakeLists.txt` (new), `driver/main.cpp` (new),
  `driver/repo_root.hpp` (new), `scripts/build_driver.sh` (new),
  `tests/andes_sim/parity.sh` (new).
- **Dependencies:** none.
- **Done when:** `bash scripts/build_driver.sh` produces `build/andes-sim`; running
  it with no args prints usage and exits non-zero; `parity.sh` runs (even if empty).

### F1 - CLI: selection axes + passthrough split + `list`
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** The two-axis arg model: `--model fast|accurate|hybrid`,
  `--engine <id>`, `--trigger csr|pc|icount|simpoint`, and the `--` boundary that
  splits framework args from verbatim engine-passthrough args. `list
  fixtures|models|engines` scaffold (`engines` may be empty until F2). `-h`.
- **Key files:** `driver/cli.{cpp,hpp}` (new), `driver/models.hpp` (new),
  `driver/cmd_list.cpp` (new). Reads `tests/fixtures/Makefile`.
- **Dependencies:** F0.
- **Done when:** `list fixtures` and `list models` match a golden table; everything
  after `--` is captured verbatim; `-h` parses for each subcommand.

### F2 - Engine registry + self-describe (plugin system + hot-plug query)  [CORE]
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** Runtime discovery: scan an engines directory, run `<bin>
  --describe`, parse the capability JSON into an `EngineDescriptor`; sidecar
  `<bin>.json` fallback; a built-in descriptor for the bundled `qemu`. `list
  engines` renders the table (the user-facing query). Add `--describe` to vsim
  (`verilator/src/main.cpp`, beside `--print-config`) emitting
  `id/type/kind/vlen(NDS_VLEN)/xlen/triggers/roles/state/invoke`. Write
  `docs/engine_interface.md` (the schema + ABI-conformance contract alioth/sid
  follow). Multi-verilator + hot-plug fall out: every built `sim_<cfg>`
  self-describes, so dropping one in makes it appear with no `andes-sim` rebuild.
- **Key files:** `driver/engine_registry.{cpp,hpp}` (new),
  `driver/engine_descriptor.hpp` (new), `driver/cmd_list.cpp` (engines),
  `verilator/src/main.cpp` (`--describe`), `docs/engine_interface.md` (new).
- **Dependencies:** F1.
- **Done when:** `andes-sim list engines` lists `qemu` plus every built `sim_<cfg>`
  with its kind/vlen/triggers; `sim_<cfg> --describe` emits valid JSON; building a
  second Verilator config makes it appear with no `andes-sim` rebuild;
  `docs/engine_interface.md` specifies the schema + ABI conformance.

### F3 - `doctor`
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** Read-only env health: artifacts, submodules, toolchain (PATH +
  `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` from env/`config.env`), runtime (nproc, `/dev/shm` free via
  statvfs). Now also lists discovered engines (uses F2). Exit 1 on any FAIL.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_doctor.cpp` (new). Reads `config.env`.
- **Dependencies:** F0 (F2 for the engine section).
- **Done when:** `doctor` matches `hsim.py` for healthy and missing-artifact states
  on the carried-over checks; the engine section reflects `list engines`.

### F4 - `build`
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** `build --what {all,qemu,vsim,plugin,simpoint,fixtures,driver}`
  plus `--dry-run`. Shells out to `scripts/build_*.sh`, `setup.sh`, `make` (allowed:
  build = setup). Inherits child stdio.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_build.cpp` (new).
- **Dependencies:** F0.
- **Done when:** `build --dry-run --what X` matches `hsim.py` for every target; a
  real `build --what plugin` succeeds.

### F5 - Infra: subprocess + passthrough-exec + mmap + state reader
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** Four foundational helpers: (1) `run_process(argv, timeout,
  capture) -> {rc, out}` (fork/exec/pipe/poll/kill) for orchestrated legs; (2)
  `exec_passthrough(argv)` that inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, applies **no
  timeout**, and propagates the child exit code - the mechanism that makes
  `fast`/`accurate` transparent (gdbstub works); (3) mmap allocator porting
  `hsim_shm` (parse_size, statvfs, mkstemp+truncate, status line); (4) state-file
  reader that `#include`s the ABI header, validates magic/version, reads
  `mcycle`/`minstret`.
- **Key files:** `driver/process.{cpp,hpp}` (new), `driver/shm.{cpp,hpp}` (new),
  `driver/state.hpp` (new). Includes `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
- **Dependencies:** F0.
- **Done when:** unit tests pass for size parsing, a timeout kill, exec-passthrough
  exit-code propagation, and a known-good state file's `mcycle`/`minstret`.

### F6 - Phase-plan engine (the executor)
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** `Step`/`Trigger`/`Plan` types and `run_plan(plan)` that loops
  steps, asks the registry for each engine's `invoke` template, fills placeholders
  (`elf`/`mmap`/`state_in`/`state_out`/trigger args), spawns via `run_process` with
  a timeout, threads the drained state file forward, and returns per-phase
  `mcycle`/`minstret`. C++ analog of `runner.run_session`, minus QEMU2.
- **Key files:** `driver/plan.hpp` (new), `driver/run_plan.{cpp,hpp}` (new),
  `driver/argv.{cpp,hpp}` (new; ports `orchestrator/spawn.py`, minus QEMU2).
- **Dependencies:** F2, F5.
- **Done when:** a 2-step hybrid plan runs end-to-end on a fixture and returns the
  expected `mcycle` delta.

### F7 - `run --model fast` (QEMU-only, transparent passthrough)
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** Resolve the `qemu` engine; take everything after `--` as QEMU
  args; `exec_passthrough` (inherit stdio, no timeout, propagate exit). gdbstub,
  `-gdb tcp::N -S`, the monitor, semihosting console all work unchanged.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_run.cpp` (new), `driver/run_passthrough.{cpp,hpp}`
  (new).
- **Dependencies:** F5, F2.
- **Done when:** `andes-sim run --model fast prog.elf -- -gdb tcp::1234 -S` behaves
  identically to raw `qemu-system-riscv64 ...` (port opens, halts, debugger
  connects); exit code propagates.

### F8 - `run --model accurate` (Verilator-only, transparent passthrough)
- **State:** DONE
- **Description:** Resolve a Verilator engine by name (`--engine verilator:<cfg>`,
  default = the sole built one); invoke `sim_<cfg>` with the ELF + `--` args and
  **no** `--resume-from-qemu` (standalone-from-reset, already supported -
  `main.cpp:436-437`). `exec_passthrough`; cycles surface in vsim's own stderr.
  Engine selection among multiple configs comes from the F2 registry.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_run.cpp`.
- **Dependencies:** F7, F2.
- **Done when:** `andes-sim run --model accurate --engine verilator:<cfg> prog.elf`
  runs the ELF from reset in vsim and the user sees vsim's native cycle line;
  selecting a different built `<cfg>` runs the other binary.

### F9 - `run --model hybrid` (orchestrated; csr|pc|icount triggers)
- **State:** NOT STARTED
- **Description:** QEMU1 drain (plugin trigger) -> vsim resume+drain
  (`--resume-from-qemu` + `--handoff-out` + shared mmap), via `run_plan`. Triggers:
  `csr` (markers), `pc` (resolve `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbol-or-`0x` by reading
  the ELF `.symtab` -> plugin `enter_pc` + vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc`), `icount`
  (plugin `icount=N` + vsim `--hybrid-icount M`). Forward extra per-leg args and
  `--kanata`/`--objdump`/`--vsim-warmup-icount`. No QEMU2. The cycle figure is the
  drained `mcycle` delta. Replaces the `tests/e2e.sh` delegation.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `driver/elf_syms.{cpp,hpp}` (new; port
  `tests/lib/roi.sh` symbol lookup).
- **Dependencies:** F6.
- **Done when:** hybrid `csr`/`pc`/`icount` produce correct vsim window cycles on
  asm + C fixtures; symbol and `0x` boundaries both resolve; matches `hsim.py`.

### F10 - `profile` + `cluster`
- **State:** NOT STARTED
- **Description:** `profile`: one QEMU+plugin BBV pass (`bbv_out`, `slice`,
  `icount`), count rows, `--dry-run`. `cluster`: run `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
  (`-loadFVFile -maxK -dim 2 -saveSimpoints -saveSimpointWeights`), report phases.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_profile.cpp` (new), `driver/cmd_cluster.cpp` (new).
- **Dependencies:** F5.
- **Done when:** `profile`/`cluster` `--dry-run` match `hsim.py`; a real profile
  emits a non-empty `.bb`; a real cluster emits simpts + weights.

### F11 - `run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint` + `estimate`
- **State:** NOT STARTED
- **Description:** Full SimPoint estimator: profile-to-exit (`drain_at_exit=1`, read
  `N_total` from `minstret`) -> cluster -> per-phase hybrid drain plans -> weighted
  CPI -> `estimated_cycles`. `estimate` is the alias. Pair simpts/weights by cluster
  id; reject `--vsim-icount 0`.
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `driver/cmd_estimate.cpp` (new),
  `driver/simpoint_phases.{cpp,hpp}` (new).
- **Dependencies:** F9, F10.
- **Done when:** `run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint --interval 100 --max-k 2`
  and `estimate` match `hsim.py`'s `estimated_cycles` on a fixture.

### F12 - `test`
- **State:** NOT STARTED
- **Description:** `test [--filter] [--mode csr|pc|both] [--jobs] [--dry-run]` wraps
  `scripts/run_e2e.sh` (allowed: testing), parses `results.tsv`, prints the
  PASS/FAIL/SKIP summary and failed-log paths, manages the temp log dir (keep on
  failure). (The QEMU2 round-trip was formerly validated here; that leg was
  removed -- `tests/e2e.sh` is now a 2-phase harness.)
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_test.cpp` (new).
- **Dependencies:** F5.
- **Done when:** `test --dry-run` matches `hsim.py`; a real `test --jobs 8` reports
  the same summary as the Python driver.

### F13 - `archive` + `replay`
- **State:** NOT STARTED
- **Description:** `archive`: port `write_archive` - copy `state.bin`, `cp
  --reflink=auto` the mem mmap, build `meta.json` (flags + vlenb from the state
  struct, ISO-8601 `captured_at`). `replay`: `--resume-with vsim` only (reuses the
  F9 vsim resume+drain primitive); `--resume-with qemu` is dropped (handback).
- **Key files:** `driver/cmd_archive.cpp` (new), `driver/cmd_replay.cpp` (new),
  `driver/meta_json.{cpp,hpp}` (new).
- **Dependencies:** F5 (F9 for replay).
- **Done when:** `archive` writes a snap dir whose `meta.json` matches the Python
  schema; `replay --resume-with vsim` drains a fixture; `--resume-with qemu` reports
  the documented "not supported" message.

### F14 - Swap + docs
- **State:** NOT STARTED
- **Description:** Make repo-root `andes-sim` the C++ binary (move Python to
  `hsim.py` as reference; retire the `hsim` name). Wire `scripts/build_driver.sh`
  into `setup.sh` and add `build --what driver`. Migrate `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh`
  -> `tests/andes_sim/`. Update `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `README.md`, and
  finalize `docs/engine_interface.md` as the "add your simulator" author guide.
- **Key files:** repo-root `andes-sim` (new binary/symlink), `hsim.py` (renamed
  reference), `setup.sh`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `README.md`,
  `docs/engine_interface.md`.
- **Dependencies:** F0-F13.
- **Done when:** `./andes-sim <subcommand>` works for every doc/test call site; the
  full parity sweep is green where defined; acceptance tests pass for the new
  surface; `andes-sim test --jobs 8` still passes the e2e suite.

---

## Behavior changes vs the old `hsim`

- New top axis `--model fast|accurate|hybrid`. The old `--mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint`
  becomes `--trigger` under `--model hybrid`.
- `fast` and `accurate` are brand-new standalone models; both are transparent
  passthroughs (full native engine CLI + I/O + exit code preserved).
- `hybrid csr|pc` prints the vsim window-cycle line (like `icount`) instead of
  `tests/e2e.sh`'s full round-trip log; the cycle number is unchanged.
- `replay --resume-with qemu` is removed; only `--resume-with vsim` remains.
- The binary is `andes-sim`; `hsim` is retired (Python kept as `hsim.py` reference
  until F14).

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
31	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
32	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
33	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
34	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
35	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
36	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
37	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
38	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
39	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
40	
41	struct PlanOptions {
42	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
43	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
44	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
45	};
46	
47	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
48	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
49	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
50	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
51	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
52	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
53	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
54	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
55	
56	}  // namespace andes_sim
57	
58	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
59

2	// port of orchestrator/spawn.py (minus QEMU2). spawn.py hand-built each argv in
3	// Python; here the argv *shape* lives in each engine's `invoke` template (from
4	// `--describe`, see docs/engine_interface.md) and build_argv fills the
5	// {placeholders} from a context map. The framework thus keeps zero per-engine

1	// andes-sim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andes-sim <cmd> [--model M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`accurate` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --model fast|accurate|hybrid
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger csr|pc|icount|simpoint
25	  std::string what;                       // --what <target> (build)
26	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
27	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
28	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
29	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
30	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
31	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
32	};

content.text:
Based on my thorough reading of the Python golden reference implementation, here is the precise map of the hybrid-run command-line behavior:

---

## 1. QEMU CSR-Mode Command Line (Exact)

**Location:** `hsim.py:725-755` (_qemu_drain_argv), `tests/e2e.sh:111-118`

**Exact structure:**
```
qemu-system-riscv64 
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=<MMAP_PATH>,size=<SIZE>"
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512
  -nographic
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native
  -bios <ELF_PATH>
  -plugin <PLUGIN_PATH>,outfile=<STATE_OUT_PATH>
```

**Inputs:** plugin_extras tuple (default empty for CSR)

---

## 2. vsim CSR-Mode Command Line (Exact)

**Location:** `hsim.py:348-365` (_vsim_drain_argv), `tests/e2e.sh:134-142`

**Exact structure:**
```
vsim <ELF_PATH>
  --resume-from-qemu <STATE_IN_PATH>
  --handoff-out <STATE_OUT_PATH>
  --shared-mem-path <MMAP_PATH>
  --shared-mem-size <SIZE>
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000
  [--hybrid-exit-pc "0x<EXIT_PC>"] (PC mode only)
  [--vsim-warmup-icount K] (F21, optional)
  [--kanata <FILE> --kanata-roi [--objdump <FILE>]] (optional)
```

**No --shared-mem-* flags for icount mode** (line 348 comment in hsim.py).

---

## 3. PC Mode: Symbol/Address Resolution and Flag Passing

**Location:** `tests/lib/roi.sh:15-47`, `tests/e2e.sh:87-90`

**Boundary resolution (resolve_pc function, roi.sh:15-21):**
- Input: symbol name OR `0x<hex>` (case-insensitive prefix)
- If `0x` or `0X` prefix: strip and use bare hex address
- If symbol: `nm --defined-only <ELF> | awk -v s="<symbol>" '$3==s{print $1}'`

def cmd_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    elf = Path(args.elf)
    if not elf.is_absolute():
        elf = (Path.cwd() / elf).resolve()
    if not elf.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: ELF not found: {args.elf}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if args.mode == "pc":
        missing = [name for name, val in
                   (("--pc-start", args.pc_start),
                    ("--pc-end", args.pc_end))
                   if not val]
        if missing:
            print(f"hsim: --mode pc requires {' and '.join(missing)} "
                  f"(symbol name or 0x address)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    if args.kanata and args.mode not in ("csr", "pc"):
        print(f"hsim: --kanata is only supported with --mode csr or pc "
              f"(got --mode {args.mode})", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.objdump and not args.kanata:
        print("hsim: --objdump requires --kanata", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    _print_run_banner(args, elf)

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./hsim build", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    if args.mode in ("csr", "pc"):
        return _run_via_e2e(elf, artifacts, args)
    if args.mode == "icount":
        return _run_drain_pair(
            elf, artifacts,
            plugin_extras=(f"icount={args.qemu_icount}",),
            vsim_icount=args.vsim_icount,
            label="icount",
            mmap_size=args.mmap_size,
            warmup_icount=args.vsim_warmup_icount,
        )
    if args.mode == "simpoint":
        if not _SIMPOINT_BIN.is_file():
            print("hsim: simpoint not built -- run ./hsim build",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        return _run_simpoint_pipeline(
            elf=elf, artifacts=artifacts,
            interval=args.interval, max_k=args.max_k,
            vsim_icount=args.vsim_icount, mmap_size=args.mmap_size,
        )
    print(f"hsim: unsupported mode: {args.mode}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2


def _run_via_e2e(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                 args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """csr/pc path: delegate to tests/e2e.sh (unchanged from F3)."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["FIXTURE"]      = elf.stem
    env["TRIGGER_MODE"] = args.mode
    env["VSIM_ELF"]     = str(elf)
    env["VSIM_BIN"]     = str(artifacts["vsim"])
    env["VSIM_QEMU"]    = str(artifacts["qemu"])
    env["VSIM_PLUGIN"]  = str(artifacts["plugin"])
    # pc mode: forward the explicit boundary PCs (symbol or 0x address).
    # Required args are validated by cmd_run before this is called.
    if args.mode == "pc":
        env["ROI_START"] = args.pc_start
        env["ROI_END"] = args.pc_end
    # ROI kanata logging: e2e.sh forwards these to vsim's --kanata /
    # --objdump / --kanata-roi flags.
    if args.kanata:
        env["KANATA_FILE"] = str(Path(args.kanata).resolve())
    if args.objdump:
        env["OBJDUMP_FILE"] = str(Path(args.objdump).resolve())
    # F21: warmup window. e2e.sh adds --vsim-warmup-icount K to the
    # vsim invocation when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set and >0, and reports the
    # captured snapshot line at the end of the run.
    if args.vsim_warmup_icount > 0:
        env["WARMUP_ICOUNT"] = str(args.vsim_warmup_icount)

    cmd = ["bash", str(REPO_ROOT / "tests" / "e2e.sh")]
    if args.verbose:
        roi = ""
        if args.mode == "pc":
            roi = f" ROI_START={env['ROI_START']} ROI_END={env['ROI_END']}"
        kanata = ""
        if args.kanata:
            kanata = f" KANATA_FILE={env['KANATA_FILE']}"
            if args.objdump:
                kanata += f" OBJDUMP_FILE={env['OBJDUMP_FILE']}"
        print(f"[hsim] FIXTURE={env['FIXTURE']} TRIGGER_MODE={env['TRIGGER_MODE']} "
              f"VSIM_ELF={env['VSIM_ELF']}{roi}{kanata}", flush=True)
        print(f"[hsim] exec: {shlex.join(cmd)}", flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, env=env,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL).returncode


# Inline QEMU + vsim drain pair for the CSR-less paths (--mode icount and
# the per-phase legs of --mode simpoint). e2e.sh only knows csr/pc
# triggers; these workloads drain at the plugin's icount/slice triggers
# and vsim exits via --hybrid-icount.
_VSIM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S = 120


def _vsim_drain_argv(vsim: Path, elf: Path, state_in: Path,
                     state_out: Path, hybrid_icount: int,
                     warmup_icount: int = 0) -> list[str]:
    """vsim drain argv with --hybrid-icount trigger.

    No --shared-mem-* flags: the CSR-less workloads re-derive their tight
    loop from the resumed state alone. `warmup_icount` is forwarded only
    when > 0 so older vsim binaries (without the flag) still accept the
    invocation -- those would error out today regardless, but keeping the
    flag out of the default argv keeps the contract narrow.
    """
    argv = [
        str(vsim), str(elf),
        "--resume-from-qemu", str(state_in),
        "--handoff-out", str(state_out),
        "--hybrid-icount", str(hybrid_icount),
    ]
    if warmup_icount > 0:
        argv += ["--vsim-warmup-icount", str(warmup_icount)]
    return argv


def _drain_round_trip(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                      plugin_extras: tuple[str, ...],
                      vsim_icount: int, label: str,
                      mmap_size: int,
                      echo_phases: bool = False,
                      warmup_icount: int = 0) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Run one QEMU + vsim drain pair, return (mcycle_qemu, mcycle_vsim).

    QEMU drains at its plugin trigger -> state file. vsim resumes from
    that state, drains after `vsim_icount` retired insns. Both spawns
    must exit `_QEMU_DRAIN_RC` (200) -- otherwise raises RuntimeError
    with the last 10 lines of the failing process's output.

    Allocates shm + two state tempfiles, unlinks them on exit (even on
    raise). `echo_phases=True` prints `[hsim <label> N/2]` status lines
    for long-running single-shot invocations (--mode icount).
    """
    shm_path = _load_hsim_shm().allocate(
        mmap_size, prefix=f"hsim-{label}-shm.",
    )
    state_q_fd, state_q_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f"hsim-{label}-qstate.")
    os.close(state_q_fd)
    state_q = Path(state_q_name)
    state_v_fd, state_v_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f"hsim-{label}-vstate.")
    os.close(state_v_fd)
    state_v = Path(state_v_name)
    try:
        if echo_phases:
            print(f"[hsim {label} 1/2] QEMU drain ({','.join(plugin_extras)})",
                  flush=True)
        qemu_argv = _qemu_drain_argv(
            artifacts["qemu"], elf, artifacts["plugin"],
            shm_path, mmap_size, state_q,
            plugin_extras=plugin_extras,
        )
        proc = subprocess.run(
            qemu_argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-10:]
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"QEMU {label} expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                f"got {proc.returncode}: " + "; ".join(tail)
            )
        mc_q = _read_state_mcycle(state_q)

        if echo_phases:
            print(f"[hsim {label} 2/2] vsim --hybrid-icount {vsim_icount} "
                  f"drain", flush=True)
        vsim_argv = _vsim_drain_argv(
            artifacts["vsim"], elf, state_q, state_v, vsim_icount,
            warmup_icount=warmup_icount,
        )
        proc = subprocess.run(
            vsim_argv, cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            timeout=_VSIM_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        if proc.returncode != _QEMU_DRAIN_RC:
            tail = proc.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()[-10:]
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"vsim {label} expected exit {_QEMU_DRAIN_RC}, "
                f"got {proc.returncode}: " + "; ".join(tail)
            )
        mc_v = _read_state_mcycle(state_v)
        return mc_q, mc_v
    finally:
        for p in (shm_path, state_q, state_v):
            try:
                p.unlink()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass


def _run_drain_pair(elf: Path, artifacts: dict[str, Path],
                    plugin_extras: tuple[str, ...],
                    vsim_icount: int, label: str,
                    mmap_size: int,
                    warmup_icount: int = 0) -> int:
    """Two-step QEMU + vsim drain round-trip with window-cycles print.

    Wraps _drain_round_trip: catches the RuntimeError on failure, prints
    PASS / window_cycles line on success. Used by --mode icount.
    """
    try:
        mc_q, mc_v = _drain_round_trip(
            elf, artifacts, plugin_extras, vsim_icount,
            label, mmap_size, echo_phases=True,
            warmup_icount=warmup_icount,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"hsim: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"[{label} window_cycles] {mc_v - mc_q}  "
          f"(vsim mcycle={mc_v} - qemu mcycle={mc_q})")
    print(f"PASS: --mode {label} ({elf.name})")
    return 0

=== tests/lib/roi.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
    return 1
  fi
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the milmb ROI markers a fixture
#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
#     ENTER = the entry marker     `csrwi milmb,0`  (encoding 7c005073)
#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker  `csrwi milmb,1`  (encoding 7c00d073)
#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
#   CSR mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT keeps
#   the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison `csrwi milmb,1`
#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
#   dead one. The encodings are unambiguous (csr 0x7c0, uimm 0/1), so the
#   raw-bytes match needs no CSR-name table from objdump.
#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
#   per-fixture config; ./hsim run still passes explicit boundaries.
roi_markers_from_disasm() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
    $2 == "7c005073" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
    $2 == "7c00d073"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
    END {
      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
      else                              { exit 1 }
    }
  '
}

def _qemu_drain_argv(qemu: Path, elf: Path, plugin: Path,
                     shm_path: Path, shm_size: int, state_out: Path,
                     plugin_extras: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]:
    """Build the QEMU + plugin drain argv.

    `plugin_extras` are `key=value` strings appended after `outfile=`.
    Same base flags as orchestrator.spawn.qemu_drain_argv; inlined here
    because that helper bakes only `outfile=` and does not yet accept
    extra plugin params.
    """
    _reject_comma("shm_path", str(shm_path))
    _reject_comma("state_out", str(state_out))
    _reject_comma("plugin", str(plugin))
    for extra in plugin_extras:
        _reject_comma("plugin_extras", extra.split("=", 1)[-1])

        f"memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,"
        f"mem-path={shm_path},size={shm_size}"

# andes-sim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andes-sim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andes-sim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_build.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andes-sim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andes-sim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andes-sim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andes-sim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andes-sim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
foreach(_t andes-sim-cli-test andes-sim-json-test andes-sim-infra-test andes-sim-plan-test andes-sim-plan-itest andes-sim-run-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
# infra/plan tests read hybrid_state_v1 via state.hpp, which includes the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andes-sim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andes-sim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andes-sim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

# F9 - `run --model hybrid` (csr | pc | icount triggers)

## Context

F9 is the next ROADMAP feature (F0-F8 done). Today `andes-sim run --model hybrid`
prints `not yet implemented`. The goal: orchestrate a real QEMU1 -> vsim handoff
for the three kernel/window triggers and print the cycle figure - matching the
Python golden `hsim`'s numbers, and replacing its `tests/e2e.sh` delegation.

Good news: **F6 already does the hard part.** `run_plan` (driver/run_plan.cpp)
spawns `[qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg]`, threads the drained
`hybrid_state_v1`, and reads each leg's `mcycle`. `plan_itest.cpp` proves the
**csr** trigger runs end-to-end and `vsim_mcycle > qemu_mcycle`. So F9 is mostly:
teach the plan the **pc** and **icount** trigger args, port the ELF symbol
lookup, add the CLI flags, and wire `cmd_run` to build+run the plan and print.

Golden behavior I verified directly (real `hsim`, not the hallucinated `hsim.py`):
- QEMU leg (all triggers): `-object memory-backend-file...` + `-plugin {plugin},outfile={state},<trig>`, exits 200. (`hsim:725-755`, `e2e.sh:111-118`)
- vsim leg: `{elf} --resume-from-qemu {in} --handoff-out {out} --shared-mem-{path,size,base} <trig>`, exits 200. (`e2e.sh:134-142`)
- Trigger args: **csr** none; **pc** plugin `,enter_pc=0x<start>` + vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<end>`; **icount** plugin `,icount=<N>` + vsim `--hybrid-icount <M>`. (`e2e.sh:85-89`, `hsim:275,361`)
- Cycle line: `[<label> window_cycles] <V-Q>  (vsim mcycle=<V> - qemu mcycle=<Q>)`. (`hsim:465`)
- pc boundary = symbol name or `0x` addr, resolved against the ELF symtab. (`tests/lib/roi.sh:15-21`)
- Defaults: qemu-icount 10000, vsim-icount 5000, mmap 128 MiB. (`hsim:1304-1342`)

## Core architecture (the one new idea: trigger -> per-leg argv)

Everything else reuses F6. A trigger contributes args to each leg, **chosen by
the leg's role**:

```
                fast-leg (qemu)                    accurate-leg (vsim)
  csr      (nothing)                          (nothing)
  pc       ,enter_pc=0x<start>  (plugin tok)  --hybrid-exit-pc 0x<end>  (extra tokens)
  icount   ,icount=<N>          (plugin tok)  --hybrid-icount <M>       (extra tokens)
```

Two mechanisms, because QEMU plugin args MUST be a comma-suffix inside the one
`-plugin` token, while vsim args are normal separate tokens:
- **qemu**: a `{trigger}` placeholder folded into the plugin token; the framework
  fills it with the comma-suffix (or `""`).
- **vsim**: extra tokens appended after the filled template.

New pure helper `leg_trigger_args(Trigger, role) -> {plugin_suffix, extra[]}` in
`run_plan.{hpp,cpp}`. `plan_argvs` calls it per step: sets `ctx["trigger"] =
plugin_suffix`, then appends `extra[]` after `build_argv`.

**Why framework-side, not in `--describe`:** the engine contract lists trigger
*names* only (`triggers: [...]`); the canonical flag spellings are framework
knowledge - the same ones the Python golden hardcodes. A per-trigger argv
template in `--describe` is a later purist extension, not F9.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andes-sim driver: driver/ -> build/andes-sim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andes-sim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andes-sim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andes-sim"

# andes-sim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andes-sim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andes-sim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_build.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andes-sim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andes-sim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andes-sim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)

add_executable(andes-sim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)

add_executable(andes-sim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)

add_executable(andes-sim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
foreach(_t andes-sim-cli-test andes-sim-json-test andes-sim-infra-test andes-sim-plan-test andes-sim-plan-itest andes-sim-run-test andes-sim-elf-syms-test)

endforeach()

# andes-sim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andes-sim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andes-sim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_build.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andes-sim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andes-sim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andes-sim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andes-sim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andes-sim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andes-sim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andes-sim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andes-sim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp)
foreach(_t andes-sim-cli-test andes-sim-json-test andes-sim-infra-test andes-sim-plan-test andes-sim-plan-itest andes-sim-run-test andes-sim-elf-syms-test andes-sim-hybrid-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
# infra/plan tests read hybrid_state_v1 via state.hpp, which includes the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andes-sim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andes-sim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andes-sim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
3	# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
4	#
5	#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
6	#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
7	#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
8	#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
9	#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
10	#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
11	#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
12	#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
13	#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
14	#      this exercises the exact argv path.
15	#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
16	#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
17	#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
18	#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
19	#      the deterministic proof.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
24	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
25	
26	BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
27	RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"
28	
29	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
30	
31	# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
32	[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
33	"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"
34	
35	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
36	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
37	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
38	
39	# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
40	# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
41	mkengine() {
42	  local f="$1/$2"
43	  cat >"$f" <<EOF
44	#!/bin/sh
45	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
46	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
47	else
48	  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
49	fi
50	EOF
51	  chmod +x "$f"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "verilator:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "verilator:f0" functional    fm

# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*verilator:v1.*verilator:v2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v1 dummy.elf
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v2 dummy.elf
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for accurate
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'verilator:nope'" \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate
expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate a.elf b.elf
# 2h. a CLI arg error is reported before (and instead of) engine discovery:
# missing ELF wins even when no engine exists, rather than "no cycle-accurate
# engine" -- so a typo never pays for a --describe subprocess per build.
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate
echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"

# 3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort)
SIM=$(ls "$ROOT"/verilator/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
  # The current fixtures are hybrid-oriented and loop forever standalone (no
  # exit path without QEMU's semihosting), so this caps the attempt: a cycle
  # line confirms the done-when; a timeout (rc 124) only confirms vsim launched
  # and is running, which is still useful. Either way -> not a failure. The cap
  # is short: the cycle line, if it comes, comes right after launch; otherwise
  # we are just confirming launch, so there is no point waiting longer.
  out=$(timeout 10 "$BIN" run --model accurate ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "[0-9]+ cycles simulated"; then
    echo "[ok] real accurate: vsim ran '$ELF' from reset, printed its cycle line (rc=$rc)"
  elif [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "[skip] real accurate: vsim launched but did not finish in 10s (expected: standalone-from-reset of a hybrid fixture has no exit path)"
  else
    echo "[skip] real accurate: vsim exited rc=$rc with no cycle line (standalone-from-reset of a hybrid fixture is env-dependent)"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real accurate run: no built sim_* and/or fixture ($SIM / $ELF)"
fi

ok "F8 run --model accurate"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint, unknown trigger"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint, unknown trigger"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint, unknown trigger"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"

+echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"
