#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andes-sim driver: driver/ -> build/andes-sim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andes-sim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andes-sim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andes-sim"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done

  || fail "HOT-PLUG: fakeB not discovered without rebuild:"$'\n'"$out"

# 6. sidecar fallback: a binary with no --describe + a <bin>.json descriptor
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc" <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 3
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc"
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc.json" <<'SIDE'
{"id":"verilator:sidecar","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":64,"xlen":64,"triggers":["icount"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}
SIDE
out=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F3 contract: `doctor` (read-only env-health).
#
#   1. The four carried-over sections (artifacts / submodules / toolchain /
#      runtime) plus the Summary line match `python3 hsim doctor` byte-for-byte,
#      including the exit code, in the ambient (healthy) env.
#   2. MISSING-ARTIFACT: a bogus VSIM_QEMU makes BOTH drivers FAIL the qemu row
#      and exit 1, with identical carried-over output.
#   3. The C++-only engines section reflects F2 discovery: the built-in qemu and
#      a hermetic fake engine both appear under `engines:`.
#
# The C++ driver appends an `engines:` readout after Summary; parity is scoped to
# the carried-over report by truncating at (and including) the `Summary:` line.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
GOLDEN="$ROOT/hsim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# The carried-over report = every line through the `Summary:` line.
carried() { awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}'; }

# 1. healthy parity (ambient env)
g=$("$GOLDEN" doctor 2>&1);  grc=$?
nf=$("$BIN" doctor 2>&1);    nrc=$?
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$nf" | carried)
[ "$grc" = "$nrc" ] || fail "doctor rc differs: golden=$grc new=$nrc"
[ "$g" = "$n" ] || {
  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$g") <(printf '%s\n' "$n") >&2
  fail "doctor carried-over output differs from golden"
}

# 2. missing-artifact: a bogus qemu path -> both FAIL the qemu row and exit 1
bogus=/nonexistent/qemu-xyz
g=$(VSIM_QEMU="$bogus" "$GOLDEN" doctor 2>&1);  grc=$?
nf=$(VSIM_QEMU="$bogus" "$BIN" doctor 2>&1);    nrc=$?
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$nf" | carried)
[ "$grc" = "1" ] || fail "golden doctor should exit 1 on missing qemu (got $grc)"
[ "$grc" = "$nrc" ] || fail "doctor rc differs (missing-artifact): golden=$grc new=$nrc"
[ "$g" = "$n" ] || {
  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$g") <(printf '%s\n' "$n") >&2
  fail "doctor carried-over output differs (missing-artifact)"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "verilator:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "verilator:f0" functional    fm

# expect: assert rc + output regex (shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*verilator:v1.*verilator:v2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v1 dummy.elf
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v2 dummy.elf
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker

#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --model hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the csr | pc | icount
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run csr/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own csr markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces csr's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=verilator:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --model hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
expect 2 'csr or pc'        "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount \
  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr \
  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden csr/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # csr -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[csr window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "csr: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --model hybrid --trigger csr ' \
    || fail "csr: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity csr "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # csr on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode csr "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity csr-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"

  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine "$ENG" \
    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after csr run"
  echo "[ok] kanata: csr run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
  rm -f "$KAN"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

ok "F9 run --model hybrid (csr|pc|icount)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F7 contract: `run --model fast` -- QEMU-only, transparent passthrough.
# Three layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): passthrough_argv fills the qemu `standalone`
#      invoke template ({bin}/{elf}) and appends the post-`--` engine args
#      verbatim -- including a `-gdb tcp::N -S` gdbstub. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. CLI error paths (no engine needed): missing --model, unknown model,
#      missing ELF, an extra positional, and engine!=qemu each exit 2 with a
#      clear message.
#   3. real passthrough (needs built qemu + a fixture): launch
#      `run --model fast ELF -- -gdb tcp::PORT -S`; the gdbstub port opens and
#      qemu halts at reset -- the done-when "port opens, halts, debugger
#      connects". exec_passthrough's exit-code propagation is already covered
#      by the F5 infra test (and observed here only indirectly).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: the argv-assembly contract carries the passthrough behavior
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (passthrough_argv) failed"

# assert `$BIN run ...` exits with $1 and its combined output matches regex $2
expect_rc_match() {
  local want_rc="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want_rc for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "output missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2. CLI error paths (deterministic; no qemu)
expect_rc_match 2 'model .* is required'    "$BIN" run
expect_rc_match 2 "unknown model 'bogus'"    "$BIN" run --model bogus p.elf
expect_rc_match 2 'missing ELF'              "$BIN" run --model fast
expect_rc_match 2 'engine args go after --'  "$BIN" run --model fast a.elf b.elf
expect_rc_match 2 "engine must be 'qemu'"    "$BIN" run --model fast --engine verilator:x p.elf

# 3. real passthrough: a frozen-at-reset gdbstub port opens (guarded on artifacts)
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  PORT=$(( 40000 + (RANDOM % 20000) ))
  BG=""
  cleanup() { [ -n "${BG:-}" ] && kill "$BG" 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "tcp::$PORT" 2>/dev/null; true; }
  trap cleanup EXIT
  # -S halts the cpu at reset, so the stub listens regardless of the ELF body.
  "$BIN" run --model fast "$ELF" -- -gdb "tcp::$PORT" -S </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  BG=$!
  opened=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    if timeout 1 bash -c ">/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PORT" 2>/dev/null; then opened=1; break; fi
    sleep 0.25
  done
  cleanup; trap - EXIT; wait "$BG" 2>/dev/null
  [ "$opened" -eq 1 ] || fail "fast passthrough: gdbstub port $PORT never opened"
  echo "[ok] real fast passthrough: qemu gdbstub halted + listening on :$PORT"
else
  echo "[skip] real fast run: qemu and/or fixture not built ($QEMU / $ELF)"
fi

# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/doctor, hidden cmds stay hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:.
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator"

# 4. list models: the composition cells read vsim, never verilator.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

## Output
- Answer is always line 1. Reasoning comes after, never before.
- No preamble. No "Great question!", "Sure!", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Absolutely!".
- No hollow closings. No "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if you need anything!".
- No restating the prompt. If the task is clear, execute immediately.
- No unsolicited suggestions. Do exactly what was asked, nothing more.

## Token Efficiency
- Compress responses. Every sentence must earn its place.
- No redundant context. Do not repeat information already established in the session.
- No long intros or transitions between sections.
- Short responses are correct unless depth is explicitly requested.

## Typography - ASCII Only
- Do not use em dashes. Use hyphens instead.
- Do not use smart or curly quotes. Use straight quotes instead.
- Do not use the ellipsis character. Use three plain dots instead.
- Do not use Unicode bullets. Use hyphens or asterisks instead.
- Do not use non-breaking spaces.
- Do not modify content inside backticks. Treat it as a literal example.

## Sycophancy - Zero Tolerance
- Never validate the user before answering.
- Never say "You're absolutely right!" unless the user made a verifiable correct statement.
- Fact-checking first, disagree when wrong. State the correction directly.
- Do not change a correct answer because the user pushes back.

## Accuracy and Speculation Control
- Never speculate about code, files, or APIs you have not read.
- If referencing a file or function: read it first, then answer.
- If unsure: say "I don't know." Never guess confidently.
- Never invent file paths, function names, or API signatures.
- If a user corrects a factual claim: accept it as ground truth for the entire session. Never re-assert the original claim.

## Code Output
- Return the simplest working solution. No over-engineering.
- No abstractions or helpers for single-use operations.
- No speculative features or future-proofing.
- No docstrings or comments on code that was not changed.
- Inline comments only where logic is non-obvious.
- Read the file before modifying it. Never edit blind.

## Warnings and Disclaimers
- No safety disclaimers unless there is a genuine life-safety or legal risk.
- No "Note that...", "Keep in mind that...", "It's worth mentioning..." soft warnings.
- No "As an AI, I..." framing.

## Session Memory
- Learn user corrections and preferences within the session.
- Apply them silently. Do not re-announce learned behavior.
- If the user corrects a mistake: fix it, remember it, move on.

## Scope Control
- Do not add features beyond what was asked.
- Do not refactor surrounding code when fixing a bug.
- Do not create new files unless strictly necessary.

## Override Rule
User instructions always override this file.

# HARD GATE - read before any edit
Before calling Edit, Write, or NotebookEdit on a non-test file, you MUST:
1. Identify the smallest behavior the change adds or fixes.
2. Have an existing failing test for that behavior visible in this session,
   either by writing one in this turn OR by running the suite and showing
   its failing output. The test must reference the behavior, not just compile.
3. State which TDD phase the next edit belongs to: RED (writing the test),
   GREEN (smallest code to pass), or REFACTOR (tests already green).

If steps 1-2 are not satisfied, STOP. Do not edit the non-test file.
Instead, write the failing test first: pick the test file, draft the
smallest test that captures the behavior, run it, and confirm it fails
for the right reason. Only then proceed to the implementation edit.


This gate applies even when the user asks to "just implement X". The
correct response is to write the test first, then implement - not to
skip the test because the user did not mention it.

# ROLE AND EXPERTISE

You are a senior software engineer who follows Test-Driven Development (TDD) and Tidy First principles. Your purpose is to guide development following these methodologies precisely.

# CORE DEVELOPMENT PRINCIPLES

- Always follow the TDD cycle: Red → Green → Refactor Refactor Refacot
- Write the simplest failing test first
- Implement the minimum code needed to make tests pass
- Refactor only after tests are passing
- Maintain high code quality throughout development, always apply the modern design patterns.
* Never workaround issues! find the real root causes and apply the proper solution. No quick fix. The slowest but proper solution is the fastest solution. is the fastest solution.
* If the code snippet needs to be changed, prefer removing all of them and rewrite completely. Don't patch the legacy code. Remove them and rewrite . Don't patch the legacy code. Remove them and rewrite. 

# TDD METHODOLOGY GUIDANCE

- Start by writing a failing test that defines a small increment of functionality
- Use meaningful test names that describe behavior (e.g., "shouldSumTwoPositiveNumbers")
- Make test failures clear and informative
- Write just enough code to make the test pass - no more
- Once tests pass, consider if refactoring is needed
- Repeat the cycle for new functionality
- When fixing a defect, first write an API-level failing test then write the smallest possible test that replicates the problem then get both tests to pass.

# When refactoring the code base: TIDY FIRST APPROACH

- Separate all changes into two distinct types:
  1. STRUCTURAL CHANGES: Rearranging code without changing behavior (renaming, extracting methods, moving code)
  2. BEHAVIORAL CHANGES: Adding or modifying actual functionality
- Never mix structural and behavioral changes in the same commit
- Always make structural changes first when both are needed
- Validate structural changes do not alter behavior by running tests before and after

# COMMIT DISCIPLINE

- Only commit when:
  1. ALL tests are passing
  2. ALL compiler/linter warnings have been resolved
  3. The change represents a single logical unit of work
  4. Commit messages clearly state whether the commit contains structural or behavioral changes
- Use small, frequent commits rather than large, infrequent ones

# CODE QUALITY STANDARDS

- Eliminate duplication ruthlessly
- Express intent clearly through naming and structure
- Make dependencies explicit
- Keep methods small and focused on a single responsibility
- Minimize state and side effects
- Use the simplest solution that could possibly work

# REFACTORING GUIDELINES

- Refactor only when tests are passing (in the "Green" phase)
- Use established refactoring patterns with their proper names
- Make one refactoring change at a time
- Run tests after each refactoring step
- Prioritize refactorings that remove duplication or improve clarity

# EXAMPLE WORKFLOW

When approaching a new feature:

1. Write a simple failing test for a small part of the feature
2. Implement the bare minimum to make it pass
3. Run tests to confirm they pass (Green)
4. Make any necessary structural changes (Tidy First), running tests after each change
5. Commit structural changes separately
6. Add another test for the next small increment of functionality
7. Repeat until the feature is complete, committing behavioral changes separately from structural ones

Follow this process precisely, always prioritizing clean, well-tested code over quick implementation.

Always write one test at a time, make it run, then improve structure. Always run all the tests (except long-running tests) each time.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test

# Parity compares the full developer surface against the golden (which exposes
# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.

pass=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# andes-sim release surface: hide "verilator", split release vs dev commands

## Context

`andes-sim` is the release product, but `--help` today exposes implementation
detail and unfinished work. Looking at `./build/andes-sim --help` the user (PM)
asked for four things:

1. Hide the word **verilator** from users (it shows in the `--help` tagline, the
   `--engine` example, `list models`, and the whole `list engines` TYPE column +
   ids like `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`).
2. Don't output **unfinished** features (`estimate`, `cluster`, `profile`, and
   the like).
3. **Separate** release features from development features.
4. The release product **shouldn't include `build` and `test`**.

Today the command table (`driver/main.cpp:35-46`) lists all 10 commands and the
help printer shows every one. Engine identity ("verilator") comes from the vsim
binary's `--describe` JSON; the driver passes it through verbatim. Selection
keys off `kind=="cycle-accurate"`, never the `type` string (`engine_registry.hpp:45`),
so relabeling the engine is safe.

Outcome: a clean release surface (`run`, `list`) that never says "verilator",
with `build`/`test`/`doctor` reachable to developers via an env var, and the
half-built ROADMAP commands hidden until they land.

## Decisions (locked)

- Replace "verilator" with **`vsim`** everywhere on the surface: TYPE column
  `vsim`, ids `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`, `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- Scrub **everywhere incl. ids** (one normalization point at discovery flips
  list / `--engine` / errors / banner together).
- Reveal dev commands via **`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1`** (release `--help` stays clean +
  one hint line; the env var adds a "developer commands" section).

**Inference to confirm at approval:** `doctor` -> **dev tier** (not release). Its
content is entirely build/setup (submodules, toolchain, `./hsim build`) and it is
the only Release command that would still print real `verilator/` paths
(`cmd_doctor.cpp:60,110`) which cannot be renamed. So Release = `run` + `list`.

## Command tiers (the one new idea)

Add `enum class Tier { Release, Dev, Hidden }` + a field on `Subcommand`
(`main.cpp:28-31`). `print_usage` shows Release; appends a Dev section only when
`ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set; Hidden is never listed. Dispatch is unchanged, so the
command surface stays stable (matches the file's stated F0 design intent).

| Tier | Commands | `--help` behavior |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| Release | `run`, `list` | always listed |
| Dev | `build`, `test`, `doctor` | listed only under `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` |
| Hidden | `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`, `replay`, `estimate` | never listed; explicit invocation still hits the existing "not yet implemented" stub |

Not in dev mode, the release help ends with one hint line:
`(set ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 to show developer commands)`.

## Change A - hide "verilator" -> "vsim"

**Single normalization point.** Add an inline helper in
`driver/engine_registry.hpp` (mirroring the existing inline `resolve_accurate_engine`):

```cpp
inline void normalize_engine_label(EngineDescriptor& d) {
  // The vsim binary self-reports the third-party simulator name; the product
  // surface speaks "vsim". One translation point so every downstream consumer
  // (list / --engine / errors / banner) sees the product id.
  if (d.type == "verilator") d.type = "vsim";
  if (d.id.rfind("verilator:", 0) == 0) d.id = "vsim:" + d.id.substr(10);
}
```

Call it in `engine_registry.cpp` `scan_dir`, right after `describe_one` succeeds
and **before** the `seen.insert(d.id)` dedup, so dedup and everything downstream
key on the product id. `builtin_qemu` ("qemu"/"qemu") is unaffected.

**Static prose** (the non-discovery sites):
- `main.cpp:56` tagline -> drop "Verilator" (e.g. "Multi-engine driver for the
  Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).").
- `main.cpp:73` `--engine` example -> `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- `models.hpp:23,25,26` (the `list models` ENGINES/NOTES cells) -> `vsim`.

**Load-bearing test filter:** `plan_itest.cpp:36` filters discovered engines by
`e.type == "verilator"` -> change to `"vsim"` (discovered engines are now vsim).

Leave: in-source code comments, and every **real filesystem path** (`verilator/build`,
`verilator/CMakeLists.txt`, `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE`) - those name the on-disk
submodule / the actual tool, not the product engine label.

## Change B - release/dev tiers

In `driver/main.cpp` only:
- `Subcommand` gains `Tier tier;`; tag each entry per the table above.
- `print_usage`: iterate Release entries; if `ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set (a small
  `is_dev_mode()` = `getenv("ANDES_SIM_DEV")` non-empty), print a
  `developer commands:` section of Dev entries; else print the hint line.
- Dispatch (`main.cpp:116-119`) unchanged. `build`/`doctor` still run; `test` +
  the Hidden five still fall through to "not yet implemented".

## Tests (strict TDD: RED first, then implement)

**1. Normalization (unit) - extend `driver/run_test.cpp`** (already includes
   `engine_registry.hpp`; no new target, no CMake change):
   - RED: assert `normalize_engine_label` maps `{type:"verilator",
     id:"verilator:ax45mpv_premium"}` -> `{vsim, vsim:ax45mpv_premium}`; leaves
     `qemu`/`qemu` and a non-verilator type (`alioth:x`) untouched. Fails to
     compile until the helper exists.
   - GREEN: add the inline helper; wire the `scan_dir` call.

**2. Release surface (acceptance) - new
   `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`** (shell, guarded like the
   other `tests/andes_sim/*` scripts, sources `tests/lib/log.sh`):
   - RED (run against the current binary first to show it fails):
     - `--help`: matches `run`,`list`; does NOT match
       `build|test|doctor|profile|cluster|archive|replay|estimate`; does NOT
       match `-i verilator`; matches the dev hint.
     - `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help`: matches `build`,`test`,`doctor`; still no
       `verilator`; still no `profile|cluster|...`.
     - `run --help`: matches `vsim:`, not `verilator:`.
     - `list models`: no `verilator`, has `vsim`.
     - `list engines` via a fake `ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR` engine that
       self-describes `"type":"verilator"` (reuse the `mkengine` pattern from
       `test_andes_sim_f8.sh`): output shows `vsim:`, never `verilator` -> proves
       the normalization end to end, deterministically, no real sim_* needed.
   - GREEN: implement A + B, rebuild, rerun -> all green.

**3. Update existing tests to the vsim contract** (the id contract changed; tests
   that encode the old label move with it):
   - Must change (discovery renames them, else they break): `test_andes_sim_f2.sh`,
     `test_andes_sim_f3.sh`, `test_andes_sim_f8.sh` (fake-engine ids + the
     `'no engine ...'` / `'multiple cycle-accurate ...'` greps), and the
     `ENG=` var in `test_andes_sim_f9.sh`.
   - Consistency (still pass, but should not show a stale label): the
     `--engine verilator:*` / id literals in `cli_test.cpp`, `run_test.cpp`,
     `plan_test.cpp`, `test_andes_sim_f7.sh`, and `json_test.cpp`'s sample
     descriptor.
   - Leave real-path refs (`verilator/build/sim_*`, `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`).

## Docs

`docs/USER_GUIDE.md`: update the **CLI-surface** references only - the command
listing, any `--engine`/engine-id example, and the `list engines` sample output
-> `vsim`. Leave the build/setup sections that legitimately discuss Verilator the
tool and the `verilator/` submodule path (lines ~87,114,177,231,285,297,303,309).

## Key files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `driver/engine_registry.hpp` | NEW inline `normalize_engine_label` |
| `driver/engine_registry.cpp` | call it in `scan_dir` before dedup |
| `driver/main.cpp` | `Tier` enum + field; tier-filtered `print_usage` + dev reveal; tagline/`--engine` prose |
| `driver/models.hpp` | `list models` cells -> `vsim` |
| `driver/run_test.cpp` | RED: normalize unit cases (+ id-literal consistency) |
| `driver/plan_itest.cpp` | `type=="vsim"` filter |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh` | NEW acceptance |
| `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f{2,3,8,9,7}.sh` | ids/greps -> `vsim` |
| `driver/{cli,plan,json}_test.cpp` | id-literal consistency |
| `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` | CLI-surface refs -> `vsim` |

## Reuse
`resolve_accurate_engine` inline pattern (model for the new inline helper),
`mkengine` fake-engine pattern (`test_andes_sim_f8.sh`), `expect`/`fail`/`ok`
(`tests/lib/log.sh`), `discover_engines`/`scan_dir` (the single seam).

## Verification
- Build: `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`
- Unit (RED then GREEN): `./build/driver/andes-sim-run-test`
- Acceptance: `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`
- Regression (vsim contract): `bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f2.sh`,
  `...f3.sh`, `...f8.sh`; and the full driver unit set
  (`for t in cli plan json run elf-syms hybrid; do ./build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test; done`)
- Manual smoke:
  `./build/andes-sim --help`  (only run/list + hint),
  `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 ./build/andes-sim --help`  (adds build/test/doctor),
  `./build/andes-sim list engines`  (vsim: ids, no "verilator")

## Commit split (when you later ask to commit)
Two behavioral units, each with its tests: (1) verilator->vsim rename +
normalization; (2) release/dev tiering. The `Tier` enum/field is introduced with
its tagging in unit (2) - no separate structural commit is warranted (it changes

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/doctor, hidden cmds stay hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:.
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator"

# 4. list models: the composition cells read vsim, never verilator.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/doctor, hidden cmds stay hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:.
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator"

# 4. list models: the composition cells read vsim, never verilator.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#   4. its kind / vlen / triggers show in `list engines`.
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.

# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-json-test"

[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests

# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.

  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
  chmod +x "$1"
}

make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "vsim:fakeA" 256

# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \

	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld

	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T test.ld $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: engine registry + self-describe (the plugin + hot-plug query).
#
#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.
#   2. the built-in qemu engine is always listed.
#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
#   4. its kind / vlen show in `list engines` (triggers are a hybrid-model
#      option, not an engine column).
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.
#
# Discovery is exercised hermetically via ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR (which REPLACES
# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-json-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests
[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"

# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.
make_engine() {  # $1=path  $2=id  $3=vlen
  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"xlen":64,"triggers":["csr","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
  chmod +x "$1"
}

ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f2.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT

make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "vsim:fakeA" 256

# 2 + 3 + 4: qemu built-in present; fakeA discovered with its fields
out=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null) \
  || fail "list engines exited non-zero"
echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu" || fail "built-in qemu not listed:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA not discovered:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "256" || fail "fakeA vlen (256) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "cycle-accurate" || fail "fakeA kind not shown:"$'\n'"$out"

# 5. hot-plug: drop a SECOND engine, re-run (no rebuild), both appear
make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeB" "vsim:fakeB" 128
out=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA missing after hot-plug"
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeB" \
  || fail "HOT-PLUG: fakeB not discovered without rebuild:"$'\n'"$out"

# 6. sidecar fallback: a binary with no --describe + a <bin>.json descriptor
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc" <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 3
OUTER
chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc"
cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc.json" <<'SIDE'
{"id":"vsim:sidecar","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":64,"xlen":64,"triggers":["icount"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}
SIDE
out=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:sidecar" \
  || fail "SIDECAR fallback failed (vsim:sidecar not listed):"$'\n'"$out"

# 7. (opportunistic) real default scan: if vsim is built, its sim_* binaries
# must self-describe and appear. Skipped when vsim has not been built.
if ls "$ROOT/verilator/build/"sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  out=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^vsim:" \
    || fail "default scan discovered no real vsim engine:"$'\n'"$out"
fi

ok "F2 engine registry + self-describe"

# andes-sim release surface: hide "verilator", split release vs dev commands

## Context

`andes-sim` is the release product, but `--help` today exposes implementation
detail and unfinished work. Looking at `./build/andes-sim --help` the user (PM)
asked for four things:

1. Hide the word **verilator** from users (it shows in the `--help` tagline, the
   `--engine` example, `list models`, and the whole `list engines` TYPE column +
   ids like `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`).
2. Don't output **unfinished** features (`estimate`, `cluster`, `profile`, and
   the like).
3. **Separate** release features from development features.
4. The release product **shouldn't include `build` and `test`**.

Today the command table (`driver/main.cpp:35-46`) lists all 10 commands and the
help printer shows every one. Engine identity ("verilator") comes from the vsim
binary's `--describe` JSON; the driver passes it through verbatim. Selection
keys off `kind=="cycle-accurate"`, never the `type` string (`engine_registry.hpp:45`),
so relabeling the engine is safe.

Outcome: a clean release surface (`run`, `list`) that never says "verilator",
with `build`/`test`/`doctor` reachable to developers via an env var, and the
half-built ROADMAP commands hidden until they land.

## Decisions (locked)

- Replace "verilator" with **`vsim`** everywhere on the surface: TYPE column
  `vsim`, ids `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`, `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
- Scrub **everywhere incl. ids** (one normalization point at discovery flips
  list / `--engine` / errors / banner together).
- Reveal dev commands via **`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1`** (release `--help` stays clean +
  one hint line; the env var adds a "developer commands" section).

**Inference to confirm at approval:** `doctor` -> **dev tier** (not release). Its
content is entirely build/setup (submodules, toolchain, `./hsim build`) and it is
the only Release command that would still print real `verilator/` paths
(`cmd_doctor.cpp:60,110`) which cannot be renamed. So Release = `run` + `list`.

## Command tiers (the one new idea)

Add `enum class Tier { Release, Dev, Hidden }` + a field on `Subcommand`
(`main.cpp:28-31`). `print_usage` shows Release; appends a Dev section only when
`ANDES_SIM_DEV` is set; Hidden is never listed. Dispatch is unchanged, so the
command surface stays stable (matches the file's stated F0 design intent).

| Tier | Commands | `--help` behavior |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| Release | `run`, `list` | always listed |
| Dev | `build`, `test`, `doctor` | listed only under `ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` |
| Hidden | `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`, `replay`, `estimate` | never listed; explicit invocation still hits the existing "not yet implemented" stub |

Not in dev mode, the release help ends with one hint line:
`(set ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 to show developer commands)`.

## Change A - hide "verilator" -> "vsim"

**Single normalization point.** Add an inline helper in
`driver/engine_registry.hpp` (mirroring the existing inline `resolve_accurate_engine`):

```cpp
inline void normalize_engine_label(EngineDescriptor& d) {
  // The vsim binary self-reports the third-party simulator name; the product
  // surface speaks "vsim". One translation point so every downstream consumer
  // (list / --engine / errors / banner) sees the product id.
  if (d.type == "verilator") d.type = "vsim";
  if (d.id.rfind("verilator:", 0) == 0) d.id = "vsim:" + d.id.substr(10);
}
```

Call it in `engine_registry.cpp` `scan_dir`, right after `describe_one` succeeds
