content.content:
1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./hsim`
35	
36	`./hsim` is the canonical end-user entry point. It wraps the
37	developer-grade scripts documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`,
38	`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind four subcommands.
39	
40	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
41	
42	```sh
43	./hsim build                                            # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
44	./hsim list fixtures                                    # discover available fixtures
45	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr     # one CSR-mode handoff
46	./hsim test                                             # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
47	```
48	
49	Expected last line of `./hsim test`:
50	
51	```
52	PASS 45, FAIL 0, SKIP 0 (elapsed: <Ns>)
53	```
54	
55	Subcommand cheat sheet:
56	
57	| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
58	|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
59	| `./hsim list <fixtures|modes>`                                   | List available fixtures or the 4 switching modes.                  |
60	| `./hsim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                       | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`. |
61	| `./hsim run <elf> --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint [-v]`            | Run one ELF through the QEMU -> vsim handoff.                       |
62	| `./hsim test [--filter REGEX] [--mode csr|pc|both] [--jobs N]`   | Run the e2e suite; defaults `--mode both --jobs 8`.                 |
63	
64	Run `./hsim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand. The rest
65	of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the underlying scripts and is
66	useful when you need to bypass `./hsim` (custom env vars, single-leg
67	debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 1. Build and environment setup
72	
73	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
74	
75	Install these on the host once:
76	
77	| Package          | Notes                                                |
78	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
79	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
80	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
81	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
82	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
83	| `python3`        | orchestrator, plugin tests                           |
84	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
85	| `pkg-config`     | QEMU configure                                       |
86	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
87	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
88	| QEMU's own deps  | pixman, slirp, ... see `QEMU/README.rst`      |
89	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
90	
91	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
92	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
93	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
94	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
95	
96	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
97	
98	```sh
99	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
100	cd hybrid_sim
101	```
102	
103	If you forgot `--recursive`:
104	
105	```sh
106	git submodule update --init --recursive
107	```
108	
109	Submodules under this repo:
110	
111	| Path             | What it is                                          |
112	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
113	| `QEMU/`   | QEMU 9.x fork that hosts the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`) |
114	| `verilator/`   | vsim sources (CMake + SystemC + Verilator)          |
115	| `tools/simpoint/`| SimPoint 3.2 clustering binary (UCSD)               |
116	
117	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
118	
119	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
120	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
121	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
122	
123	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
124	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
125	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
126	`config.env`:
127	
128	```sh
129	# config.env
130	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
131	```
132	
133	The single variable today is:
134	
135	| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
136	|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
137	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
138	
139	How it propagates:
140	
141	- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
142	  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
143	- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
144	  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
145	  the variable is missing.
146	- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
147	  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives
148	  `NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`.
149	
150	Override per-invocation without editing the file:
151	
152	```sh
153	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain make -C tests/fixtures
154	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain ./hsim run \
155	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode pc \
156	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>  # see docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md
157	```
158	
159	### 1.4 Build everything
160	
161	One command builds all four artifacts and exports the env vars the
162	test harness expects:
163	
164	```sh
165	source ./setup.sh
166	```
167	
168	`source` (not `bash`) is required so the script can prepend the build
169	dirs to PATH and export `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `VSIM_BIN`,
170	`SIMPOINT_BIN`, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` into the current shell. The steps it
171	runs:
172	
173	```
174	0/4 config     -> auto-copy config.env.example -> config.env (first run);
175	                  source it; export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
176	1/4 QEMU       -> build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
177	2/4 vsim       -> verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium    (in container)
178	3/4 plugin     -> qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
179	4/4 SimPoint   -> tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
180	```
181	
182	To rebuild just one component:
183	
184	```sh
185	./scripts/build_qemu.sh
186	./scripts/build_vsim.sh        # uses podman + Dockerfile (target `env`)
187	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU
188	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh
189	```
190	
191	To clean:
192	
193	```sh
194	source ./setup.sh clean         # all four
195	source ./setup.sh clean qemu    # just QEMU build/
196	source ./setup.sh clean vsim
197	source ./setup.sh clean plugin
198	source ./setup.sh clean simpoint
199	```
200	
201	### 1.5 Build the test fixtures (RISC-V ELFs)
202	
203	Fixtures are small RISC-V programs that exercise specific transport
204	paths. They are NOT built by `setup.sh`; build them once:
205	
206	```sh
207	make -C tests/fixtures -j
208	```
209	
210	One fixture at a time:
211	
212	```sh
213	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul.elf
214	```
215	
216	Output ELFs land next to the sources under
217	`tests/fixtures/*.elf`. The fixtures depend on the Andes
218	RISC-V GCC + the `libgloss_vh` semihosting library. The toolchain path
219	comes from `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` (see section 1.3); to override for one
220	invocation:
221	
222	```sh
223	make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain
224	```
225	
226	### 1.6 Sanity check the build
227	
228	```sh
229	# All four artifacts present?
230	ls build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
231	ls verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
232	ls qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
233	ls tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
234	
235	# Smallest possible end-to-end - one CSR-mode handoff:
236	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr TIMEOUT=120 \
237	  bash tests/e2e.sh
238	```
239	
240	Expected last line:
241	
242	```
243	[rt_c_v_matmul PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)
244	```
245	
246	If you see `skip: ... not built`, redo `source ./setup.sh` and
247	re-build fixtures (`make -C tests/fixtures`).
248	
249	---
250	
251	## 2. Configuring the simulator
252	
253	There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
254	vars in 2.1.
255	
256	### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)
257	
258	`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
259	somewhere non-default.
260	
261	| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
262	|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
263	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
264	| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`                 | every harness            |
265	| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
266	| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `verilator/build/sim_*`                  | every harness            |
267	| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
268	| `SIMPOINT_BIN`  | `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`                    | SimPoint pipeline        |
269	| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
270	| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (120 for long runs)                         | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
271	| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
272	| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `csr`                                            | `csr` or `pc`            |
273	| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
274	| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` | `/dev/shm`                                       | backing dir for `--mmap-size`; redirect when /dev/shm too small |
275	
276	Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:
277	
278	```sh
279	VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
280	  ./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode csr
281	```
282	
283	### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML
284	
285	`verilator/config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The
286	default is `ax45mpv_premium`:
287	
288	```yaml
289	cpus:
290	  ax45mpv_premium:
291	    cpu_series: 45
292	    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
293	    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
294	    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
295	    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
296	    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
297	    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
298	```
299	
300	Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML:
301	
302	```sh
303	cd verilator
304	cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml

311	### 2.3 QEMU plugin args
312	
313	The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
314	select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:
315	
316	| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
317	|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
318	| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
319	| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | PC mode: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the CSR-insn matcher.         |
320	| `icount=N`           | icount mode: drain on the N-th retired insn (per vcpu).                |
321	| `bbv_out=PATH`       | SimPoint: emit one BBV row per `slice=N` insns into PATH.              |
322	| `slice=N`            | Insns per slice (used by the SimPoint stages). Must be > 0.            |
323	| `slice_at=K`         | SimPoint slice stage: drain at the end of the K-th slice (needs `slice=N`). |
324	| `drain_at_exit=1`    | Drain when QEMU exits naturally; overrides `minstret` with a plugin-side per-insn counter. Used by `./hsim run --mode simpoint` (and `./hsim estimate`) to read true `N_total`. |
325	
326	If no mode arg is given, the default is CSR-insn match (CSR mode): the
327	plugin matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire.
328	
329	Example invocation (CSR mode, just the minimal arg):
330	
331	```
332	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
333	```
334	
335	Example (icount mode):
336	
337	```
338	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin,icount=10000
339	```

341	### 2.4 vsim CLI flags
342	
343	`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:
344	
345	| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
346	|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
347	| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
348	| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
349	| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
350	| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
351	| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
352	| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | PC mode exit: drain when this PC retires.               |
353	| `--hybrid-icount N`           | icount mode exit: drain after N committed insns (vsim).  |
354	| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (e.g. OpenOCD).              |
355	| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |
356	
357	Defaults for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the QEMU `virt` /
358	`andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.
359	
360	Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
361	license-gated and off by default).

363	### 2.5 Requesting more memory (`--mmap-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)
364	
365	By default every `./hsim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
366	a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
367	workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
368	RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:
369	
370	| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
371	|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
372	| `--mmap-size SPEC` | flag on `run`, `profile`, `archive`, `estimate` | request a larger mmap (`SPEC` = `128M`, `8G`, `1.5G`, `2T`, or raw bytes). Default `128M`. |
373	| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | override the backing directory (default `/dev/shm`). |
374	
375	Selection rule is deliberately simple: if `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` is set we
376	use it, otherwise `/dev/shm`. We check free space via `statvfs` and
377	error rc=2 with a clear hint if the pinned dir can't hold the request.
378	There is **no fallback chain** -- we never silently switch directories
379	on you.
380	
381	Examples:
382	
383	```sh
384	# Small request; default backend is /dev/shm.
385	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr --mmap-size 256M
386	
387	# 8 GiB request that won't fit /dev/shm: redirect to a disk-backed dir.
388	HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch/hsim \
389	  ./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode icount --mmap-size 8G
390	
391	# Each allocation prints one status line:
392	#   [hsim mmap] 8.0 GiB at /scratch/hsim (free: 64.0 GiB)
393	```
394	
395	If your `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch default), pointing
396	`HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` is fine **only** if `/tmp` has enough free bytes;
397	otherwise pick a directory on a non-tmpfs filesystem (`/var/tmp`,
398	`$HOME/.cache/hsim`, `/scratch`, etc.).
399	
400	The hardcoded `mktemp -p /dev/shm` paths in the shell harnesses
401	(`tests/e2e.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) all use
402	128 MiB and are unaffected.

437	## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use
438	
439	| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
440	|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
441	| CSR      | a kernel          | `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |
442	| PC       | a kernel          | PC equals a boundary: any symbol or `0x` address (both `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` required) | kernel cycles |
443	| icount   | a sampled window  | N retired insns (single boundary; no markers)            | window cycles          |
444	| SimPoint | the whole program | clustering picks representative slices, each measured like icount | whole-program estimate |
445	
446	CSR/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose; icount/SimPoint sample the whole
447	program by instruction count (SimPoint is icount repeated, weight-combined).
448	How each is driven: every mode goes through `./hsim run --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint`
449	(simpoint is also exposed as `./hsim estimate`). The cycle figure is always
450	the vsim `mcycle` delta (offset 624); SimPoint extrapolates many deltas
451	into `estimated_cycles`.
452	
453	Decision flow:
454	
455	```
456	Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
457	  binary is yours to edit          -> CSR  (csrwi 0x7C0,0/1 around the kernel)
458	  not editable, symbol/PC at ends  -> PC   (./hsim run --mode pc
459	                                            --pc-start S --pc-end E)
460	Profiling the WHOLE program (or a CSR-less blob)?
461	  one window by instruction count  -> icount
462	  representative phases, combined  -> SimPoint  (./hsim run --mode simpoint)
463	```
464	
465	> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (CSR/PC modes):** keep the measured
466	> kernel anchored inside the `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` span -- read its inputs and
467	> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
468	> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
469	> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
470	> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
471	> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
472	> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.
473

497	### 4.1 CSR mode - the default (kernel)
498	
499	Goal: run a vector fixture through QEMU1 -> vsim using the
500	two `csrwi 0x7C0, *` markers that the fixture already contains.
501	
502	```sh
503	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode csr
504	```
505	
506	Expected last line:
507	
508	```
509	[rt_c_v_matmul PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)
510	```
511	
512	`hsim run --mode csr` is a thin Python wrapper around the generic
513	`tests/e2e.sh` harness. Inside, the two legs are:
514	
515	```
516	1) QEMU1 with -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE
517	        -> drain at csrwi 0x7C0,0   -> exit 200
518	2) sim_ax45mpv_premium $ELF \
519	        --resume-from-qemu $STATE --handoff-out $STATE_V \
520	        --shared-mem-path $SHM --shared-mem-size 128MB
521	        -> ROI runs in vsim, drains at csrwi 0x7C0,1   -> exit 200
522	```
523	
524	Try a different fixture:
525	
526	```sh
527	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf --mode csr
528	```
529	
530	### 4.2 PC mode - markerless workload, explicit boundary PCs
531	
532	Same plumbing as CSR mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers.
533	The user picks the switch PCs explicitly via `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`,
534	each a symbol name or `0x` address. Both args are required for `--mode pc`.
535	
536	```sh
537	# resolve the boundary PCs once (cheap, host-side; needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
538	ELF=tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf
539	START=vmatmul_kernel
540	END=$(${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d "$ELF" \
541	        | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
542	        | tr -d ':')
543	
544	./hsim run "$ELF" --mode pc --pc-start "$START" --pc-end "$END"
545	```
546	
547	`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the **markerless twin** of the GEMM fixture,
548	built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same source as the marked
549	`rt_c_v_matmul`. Both triggers are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on
550	first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is
551	**exactly one full `vmatmul_kernel` call** (16 outer rows + inner k-loop
552	+ vse32 stores). The cycle count should land near CSR mode's ~22808.
553	
554	The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
555	address. Under `tests/e2e.sh` the same knobs are the `ROI_START` /
556	`ROI_END` env vars; `hsim run --mode pc` forwards `--pc-start` / `--pc-end`
557	into those env vars for you.
558	
559	To see what `hsim run --mode pc` passes under the hood:
560	
561	```sh
562	# Resolve the boundaries (objdump-based; pick any two PCs in the ELF):
563	OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
564	NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm
565	ROI_START=$("$NM" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
566	              | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print "0x"$1}')
567	ROI_END=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
568	              | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
569	              | tr -d ':')
570	echo "enter=$ROI_START  exit=$ROI_END"   # e.g. 0x10021c / 0x1002cc
571	
572	# QEMU1 leg
573	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
574	  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
575	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
576	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
577	  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
578	  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
579	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=$ROI_START"
580	
581	# vsim leg
582	"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
583	  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
584	  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
585	  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
586	  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
587	  --hybrid-exit-pc "$ROI_END"
588	```
589	
590	The fixture binary differs from CSR mode (markerless vs marked), and the
591	QEMU1 plugin and vsim flags carry hex PCs (`enter_pc=` / `--hybrid-exit-pc`)
592	instead of CSR-trigger plumbing.
593	
594	### 4.3 icount mode - a sampled window (no markers)
595	
596	For workloads you cannot edit. Both legs switch on a retired-insn count -
597	a **single boundary** on each side: QEMU fast-forwards `--qemu-icount` insns,
598	vsim measures `--vsim-icount` insns and drains. The cycle figure (window
599	cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU `mcycle`, offset 624) is the raw vsim-side
600	delta. Pair it with `--vsim-warmup-icount K` (see "Warmup window" below)
601	to exclude the first K cold-cache insns from the reported figure.
602	
603	```sh
604	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode icount \
605	  --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 1000
606	```
607	
608	Override the targets directly on the command line (defaults: 10000 / 5000):
609	
610	```sh
611	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode icount \
612	  --qemu-icount 20000 --vsim-icount 8000
613	```
614	
615	Use the markerless GEMM (`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf`) - the twin of the marked
616	GEMM, built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same source. icount mode needs
617	the markers compiled out: the plugin's CSR matcher stays live, so a
618	`csrwi 0x7C0,0` would drain at the marker before the icount target is
619	reached.
620	
621	What you can verify by hand: extract the drained PC from
622	`state.bin` at byte offset 16, little-endian u64, and asserts it lands inside
623	`vmatmul_kernel` (resolve the range with `readelf -sW ... | awk
624	'$8=="vmatmul_kernel"'`; it sits at `0x10021c..0x100274`):
625	
626	```sh
627	python3 -c "
628	import struct
629	print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', open('/tmp/icount_state.bin','rb').read()[16:24])[0]))
630	"
631	```

633	### 4.4 SimPoint-driven mode (whole program)
634	
635	Real programs are too long to cycle-simulate end to end. SimPoint samples:
636	profile the run into fixed slices, cluster them into a few representative
637	phases, measure each phase like icount mode, then weight-combine into a
638	whole-program cycle estimate. **SimPoint mode is icount mode repeated** at
639	clustering-chosen points. The headline command is
640	`./hsim run --mode simpoint` (or equivalently `./hsim estimate`); the
641	stages below show the underlying pieces for debugging.
642	
643	#### Stage 1: BBV profile pass
644	
645	QEMU1 emits one BBV row per slice; the offline `simpoint` tool
646	clusters them. No vsim leg.
647	
648	```sh
649	./hsim profile tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
650	  --slice 1000 --icount 10000 -o /tmp/profile.bb
651	```
652	
653	Plugin args under the hood:
654	
655	```
656	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,bbv_out=/tmp/profile.bb,slice=1000,icount=10000
657	```
658	
659	That writes 10 BBV rows (`icount / slice`). Then:
660	
661	```sh
662	./hsim cluster /tmp/profile.bb --max-k 2 \
663	  --simpts /tmp/simpts --weights /tmp/weights
664	```
665	
666	`simpts` lines: `<slice_idx> <cluster_id>`. `weights` lines:
667	`<mass> <cluster_id>`.
668	
669	#### Stage 2: per-phase drain
670	
671	Given a `K` chosen from Stage 1's `simpts` output, drain QEMU at the END
672	of slice K so vsim resumes from exactly that point. The headline
673	`./hsim run --mode simpoint` performs this per-phase drain automatically
674	for every cluster representative; the lower-level plumbing is:
675	
676	```
677	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,slice=1000,slice_at=3,icount=10000
678	```
679	
680	`icount=` is a safety fallback if K is invalid.
681	
682	#### Stage 3: archive checkpoint and replay
683	
684	Capture a portable archive `snap/0/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` from a
685	single QEMU drain, then resume it on vsim in a separate
686	process. `./hsim archive` packages an existing drained state file +
687	mmap; `./hsim replay` hydrates the archive and resumes.
688	
689	```sh
690	# First produce a state.bin + mmap from any earlier drain (e.g. via run),
691	# then bundle them into a portable snapshot directory:
692	./hsim archive --state /tmp/state.bin --mmap /tmp/share \
693	  --elf tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf -o /tmp/m6m7/snap/0
694	
695	# Replay on vsim:
696	./hsim replay /tmp/m6m7/snap/0 --resume-with vsim
697	```
698	
699	The orchestrator commands you can run by hand:
700	
701	```sh
702	python3 -m orchestrator.main run plan.yaml \
703	  --project-root . \
704	  --workdir /tmp/m6m7/run \
705	  --archive-root /tmp/m6m7
706	# -> /tmp/m6m7/snap/0/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}
707	
708	python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint /tmp/m6m7/snap/0 \
709	  --resume-with vsim \
710	  --project-root . \
711	  --workdir /tmp/m6m7/replay
712	```
713	
714	#### Stage 4: `./hsim estimate` - whole-program cycle estimate (the headline)
715	
716	`./hsim run --mode simpoint <elf>` (or the equivalent `./hsim estimate
717	<elf>`) runs the full pipeline (BBV profile -> SimPoint cluster ->
718	per-phase QEMU+vsim drain) and aggregates a weighted CPI to project a
719	cycle count for the whole program:
720	
721	```sh
722	./hsim run gemm.elf --mode simpoint --interval 5000 --max-k 4
723	# or, the lower-level alias:
724	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 5000 --max-k 4
725	```
726	
727	(`./hsim run --mode simpoint` uses `--interval`; `./hsim estimate` keeps
728	the historical `--slice` name. Both name the same "insns per slice"
729	parameter.)
730	
731	The profile pass **always runs the program to its natural exit** (e.g.
732	libgloss_vh semihosting EXIT). The plugin counts every retired insn via a
733	per-insn TCG callback and writes that count into the drained state file's
734	`minstret` field; hsim uses it as `N_total` in:
735	
736	```
737	CPI_i           = delta_mcycle_i / vsim_icount
738	weighted_CPI    = sum_i ( w_i * CPI_i )
739	estimated_cycles = N_total * weighted_CPI
740	```
741	
742	Example output (gemm.elf, ~254K insns):
743	
744	```
745	profile: 4 BBV rows -> .../profile.bb (N_total=254391)
746	cluster: 4 phases
747	phase K=0 w=0.020 delta_mcycle=48105 CPI=9.621
748	phase K=4 w=0.940 delta_mcycle=58621 CPI=11.724
749	...
750	estimated_cycles=2955387  (N=254391, weighted_CPI=11.617)
751	```
752	
753	Caveats:
754	
755	- The fixture must reach `_exit` (return from `main`, or call `exit(0)`).
756	  Programs that hang in an infinite loop will hit the QEMU 30s profile
757	  timeout; simpoint mode is not designed for non-exiting workloads --
758	  cap them at the source or use a different mode (icount).
759	- The fixture must be **markerless** (no `csrwi 0x7C0,*`). The plugin's
760	  CSR matcher is still armed in simpoint mode and would drain at the
761	  first marker before natural exit, cutting `N_total` short.
762	- The ELF must be linked at the andes_ae350 `-bios` load address
763	  (`0x00100000`); use the linker script `tests/fixtures/test.ld` or the
764	  fixture Makefile. ELFs at other addresses won't execute.
765	
766	#### How to pick `--slice` and `--max-k`
767	
768	These two flags trade profile granularity against vsim cost. Here is the
769	short version; the rest of this section explains why.
770	
771	```
772	slice  ~= N_total / 20         # aim for ~20 BBV rows
773	max-k  =  2                    # start simple, increase only if needed
774	```
775	
776	**Two-step workflow.** First run with defaults to learn N_total, then
777	re-run with a tuned slice:
778	
779	```sh
780	./hsim estimate myprog.elf
781	# read the line:  profile: <rows> BBV rows ... (N_total=<N>)
782	# then:
783	./hsim estimate myprog.elf --slice $((N/20))
784	```
785	
786	**Picking `--slice`** (insns per BBV row). One BBV row is the smallest
787	unit SimPoint can cluster. Too few rows -> k-means cannot find structure.
788	Too many rows -> long profile pass and long clustering. Aim for ~20.
789	
790	| Program size (N_total) | Pick `--slice`  |
791	|------------------------|-----------------|
792	| < 10K (toy)            | 500             |
793	| 10K..100K              | 1000..5000      |
794	| 100K..1M               | 5000..50000     |
795	| > 1M                   | 50000+          |
796	
797	**Picking `--max-k`** (number of phases). Each phase costs **one extra
798	QEMU+vsim drain pair** (~5..10s). SimPoint will sometimes pick fewer
799	phases than `--max-k` if the workload is uniform, so `max-k` is an upper
800	bound, not a fixed count.
801	
802	| Workload structure              | Pick `--max-k` |
803	|---------------------------------|----------------|
804	| Single loop kernel              | 2 (init + body) |
805	| Init + kernel + cleanup         | 3              |
806	| Multi-kernel (e.g. 2 GEMMs)     | 4..6           |
807	| Large benchmark mix             | 8..16          |
808	
809	**Sanity checks after a run.** Read the per-phase rows and apply:
810	
811	1. `BBV rows >= 2 * max_k`. If fewer, drop `--slice` so more rows fit.
812	2. Weights add to ~1.0 and are not all small. If all `--max-k` phases
813	   have similar weights, the workload is uniform and you can drop `max_k`.
814	3. CPIs differ across phases. If every phase reports the same CPI, you
815	   are paying for vsim time without gaining accuracy. Drop `max_k`.
816	
817	**Worked example: gemm.elf** (N_total = 254391):
818	
819	```sh
820	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 5000 --max-k 4
821	# Output:
822	# profile: 4 BBV rows -> .../profile.bb (N_total=254391)
823	# phase K=0 w=0.020 ...   phase K=1 w=0.020 ...
824	# phase K=2 w=0.020 ...   phase K=4 w=0.940 CPI=11.724
825	```
826	
827	`slice=5000` gave only 4 BBV rows -- too few for `max_k=4`. The weights
828	also tell you one phase (K=4, the GEMM kernel) accounts for 94% of the
829	program; the other three are startup. A cleaner setup:
830	
831	```sh
832	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 10000 --max-k 2
833	# slice=10000 -> ~25 BBV rows; max_k=2 -> startup + kernel only
834	```
835	
836	**One-line rule.** Start with `--slice $((N_total/20)) --max-k 2`. Raise
837	`max_k` only when a single dominant phase (w > 0.8) hides sub-phase
838	detail you care about.
839	
840	#### Headline demo: the full loop
841	
842	One command chains all four phases on the **markerless** GEMM twin
843	(simpoint requires a markerless workload that exits naturally):
844	
845	```sh
846	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode simpoint \
847	  --interval 100 --max-k 2
848	```
849	
850	Expected last line: `estimated_cycles=<positive integer>`.
851	
852	For a different fixture, swap the ELF (must be markerless + exit-clean)
853	and tune `--interval` so the BBV pass yields 10..30 rows
854	(`--interval ~= N_total / 20`):
855	
856	```sh
857	./hsim run tests/fixtures/my_workload.elf --mode simpoint \
858	  --interval 50 --max-k 3
859	```
860	
861	### 4.5 Warmup window - drop cold-cache cycles from the report
862	
863	Every cycle figure above (csr / pc / icount / simpoint) treats the entire
864	vsim window as the measured region. The first few thousand vsim insns hit
865	cold caches/BPU/TLB and run slower than steady state; if you only care
866	about the warm-cache cost, those cycles are noise. Pass
867	`--vsim-warmup-icount K` to anchor a measurement-start snapshot K committed
868	insns after vsim entry. The orchestrator then reports a 3-way split:
869	
870	```
871	warmup:    K_cycles cycles   K_insns insns      (cold prefix)
872	measure:   M_cycles cycles   M_insns insns      (warm tail, this is the
873	                                                 ROI-final figure)
874	total:     T_cycles cycles   T_insns insns      (sum, matches the no-warmup
875	                                                 single figure)
876	```
877	
878	Mechanism: the snapshot stays inside one vsim process so caches do not
879	get flushed - only the stats window moves. K=0 (default) reproduces the
880	no-warmup behaviour bit-for-bit. The K-th-commit boundary is captured via
881	a Debug-Module halt + abstract-command read of `mcycle` / `minstret` at
882	the moment the counter trips, then vsim resumes; in CSR / PC mode the
883	snapshot lands on exactly the K-th retire, in icount mode it can be off
884	by a handful of insns because ResumeDriver injects Program-Buffer ops
885	that bump the hart-side minstret without going through the trigger.
886	
887	```sh
888	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
889	  --mode csr --vsim-warmup-icount 1000
890	
891	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
892	  --mode icount --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 5000 \
893	  --vsim-warmup-icount 1000     # require K < --vsim-icount
894	```
895	
896	The warmup pair lands in the drained state file at the F13 ABI offsets
897	`mcycle_at_measure_start` (offset 3392) and `minstret_at_measure_start`
898	(offset 3400); both remain zero when K=0 or the workload exited inside
899	the warmup window. The csr/pc e2e wrapper prints a
900	`[<fixture> warmup] K=K mcycle_at_measure_start=...` line; the
901	orchestrator's `run` subcommand prints the 3-way breakdown per step.
902	
903	Coming from gem5: this is the analogue of `--warmup-insts N` followed by
904	an implicit `m5.stats.reset()`. The constraint differs - QEMU has no
905	cache model, so unlike gem5 the warmup MUST happen inside the cycle-
906	accurate phase (vsim). Otherwise the contract is identical: K cold
907	insns, then the measured window.
908	
909	### 4.6 Capturing a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI
910	
911	When debugging a hot path on vsim, pass `--kanata FILE` to `./hsim run`
912	in csr or pc mode. The resulting trace contains pipeline records only
913	for the ROI region (between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain) -- vsim
914	boot and DMI resume overhead are filtered out.
915	
916	```sh
917	# csr mode: the ROI is the span between the two csrwi 0x7C0,{0,1}
918	# markers already in the source. vsim auto-derives the window.
919	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
920	  --mode csr --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
921	
922	# pc mode: the ROI bounds are whatever PCs you passed.
923	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
924	  --mode pc --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc \
925	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
926	```
927	
928	Add `--objdump FILE` so the kanata `L` records embed the disassembly
929	text next to each PC. Generate the dump once with the toolchain
930	`objdump -d`:
931	
932	```sh
933	$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
934	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf > /tmp/roi.S
935	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
936	  --mode csr --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata --objdump /tmp/roi.S
937	```
938	
939	Open `/tmp/roi.kanata` in [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata)
940	to view the pipeline.
941	
942	Constraints:
943	
944	- `--kanata` is only valid with `--mode csr` or `--mode pc`. icount and
945	  simpoint modes have no single ROI-exit PC; they are rejected with
946	  rc=2.
947	- csr mode requires exactly one `csrwi 0x7C0,1` (exit marker) in the
948	  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
949	  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode pc with explicit --pc-end`.
950	  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
951	- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
952	
953	How it works:
954	
955	- hsim forwards `KANATA_FILE` (and optionally `OBJDUMP_FILE`) to
956	  `tests/e2e.sh`, which appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
957	  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
958	- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
959	  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
960	  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
961	  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
962	  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
963	    `csrwi 0x7C0,1` PC from CsrTrigger (csr mode)
964	  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
965	    close on first retire of end_pc).
966	
967	---
968	
969	## 5. Running the full test suite
970	
971	After any change to the simulator or plugin, run the suite:
972	
973	```sh
974	JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
975	```
976	
977	`JOBS=8` is the practical cap on this 128-core host (vsim Verilator
978	processes are CPU-hungry; the default cap of 128 saturates the box and
979	times out). Logs go to `/tmp/e2e-<RAND>/`; failed-test logs are
980	streamed at the end.
981	
982	Run a subset:
983	
984	```sh
985	FILTER=rt_c_v JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh        # only V-related fixtures
986	MODE=csr     JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # skip the pc-mode iterations
987	JOBS=1                     bash scripts/run_e2e.sh  # sequential for debugging
988	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs       bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
989	```
990	
991	For a per-mode handoff on the GEMM workload, drive `./hsim run`
992	directly (`--mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint`); see Section 4 for the
993	mode-by-mode commands.
994	
995	The e2e suite runs via `scripts/run_e2e.sh`, not CTest; the vsim submodule
996	registers only the hybrid-layer doctest unit tests (there is no
997	`switching-mode` CTest label).
998	
999	---
1000	
1001	## 6. Common failures and how to read them
1002	
1003	| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
1004	|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
1005	| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |
1006	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC / wrong icount value.     |
1007	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                    | `timeout` killed the plugin. Increase `TIMEOUT` or tune the target.  |
1008	| `cannot resolve ROI start/end '<x>'`                   | PC-mode boundary `<x>` is neither a `0x` address nor a defined symbol. Fix `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`), or use CSR mode. |
1009	| `vsim drained pc=0x... not in vmatmul_kernel`          | `VSIM_ICOUNT`/`QEMU_ICOUNT` too small (count target lands before the kernel) or wrong fixture for icount mode. |
1010	| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
1011	| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |
1012	
1013	---
1014	
1015	## 7. Where to go next
1016	
1017	- `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md` - architecture deep-dive (state ABI,
1018	  Debug Module transport, V-scratch trick, passthrough rationale).
1019	- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` - one exercise per mode with
1020	  drill-down on the underlying CLI invocations.
1021	- `CLAUDE.md` - file-level pointers (key files, build commands,
1022	  fixture authoring rules).
1023	- `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` - the RVV GEMM the four switching modes
1024	  run; one source builds both the marked (kernel modes) and markerless
1025	  (count modes) variants.
1026	- `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.c` - reference fixture for V-regfile transport
1027	  (V regfile + V scalar CSRs + shared memory).
1028	- `gemm_modes.md` - why the four modes share one GEMM workload, marked vs markerless.
1029

# Hybrid Simulator User Guide

Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
not study its internals. After this guide you can:

1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
   with a concrete worked example.

For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.

---

## 0. The one-paragraph mental model

QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
hands control between them. One run is two legs:

```
   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
```

The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
mode".

---

## 0.5 Quick start with `./hsim`

`./hsim` is the canonical end-user entry point. It wraps the
developer-grade scripts documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`,
`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind four subcommands.

Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:

```sh
./hsim build                                            # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
./hsim list fixtures                                    # discover available fixtures
./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr     # one CSR-mode handoff
./hsim test                                             # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
```

Expected last line of `./hsim test`:

```
PASS 45, FAIL 0, SKIP 0 (elapsed: <Ns>)
```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `./hsim list <fixtures|modes>`                                   | List available fixtures or the 4 switching modes.                  |
| `./hsim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                       | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`. |
| `./hsim run <elf> --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint [-v]`            | Run one ELF through the QEMU -> vsim handoff.                       |
| `./hsim test [--filter REGEX] [--mode csr|pc|both] [--jobs N]`   | Run the e2e suite; defaults `--mode both --jobs 8`.                 |

Run `./hsim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand. The rest
of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the underlying scripts and is
useful when you need to bypass `./hsim` (custom env vars, single-leg
debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).

---

## 1. Build and environment setup

### 1.1 Host prerequisites

Install these on the host once:

| Package          | Notes                                                |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
| `python3`        | orchestrator, plugin tests                           |
| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
| `pkg-config`     | QEMU configure                                       |
| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
| QEMU's own deps  | pixman, slirp, ... see `QEMU/README.rst`      |
| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |

The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.

### 1.2 Clone with submodules

```sh
git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
cd hybrid_sim
```

If you forgot `--recursive`:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Submodules under this repo:

| Path             | What it is                                          |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `QEMU/`   | QEMU 9.x fork that hosts the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`) |
| `verilator/`   | vsim sources (CMake + SystemC + Verilator)          |
| `tools/simpoint/`| SimPoint 3.2 clustering binary (UCSD)               |

### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)

The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).

On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
`config.env`:

```sh
# config.env
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
```

The single variable today is:

| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |

How it propagates:

- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
  the variable is missing.
- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives
  `NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`.

Override per-invocation without editing the file:

```sh
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain make -C tests/fixtures
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain ./hsim run \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode pc \
  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>  # see docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md
```

### 1.4 Build everything

One command builds all four artifacts and exports the env vars the
test harness expects:

```sh
source ./setup.sh
```

`source` (not `bash`) is required so the script can prepend the build
dirs to PATH and export `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `VSIM_BIN`,
`SIMPOINT_BIN`, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` into the current shell. The steps it
runs:

```
0/4 config     -> auto-copy config.env.example -> config.env (first run);
                  source it; export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
1/4 QEMU       -> build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
2/4 vsim       -> verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium    (in container)
3/4 plugin     -> qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
4/4 SimPoint   -> tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
```

To rebuild just one component:

```sh
./scripts/build_qemu.sh
./scripts/build_vsim.sh        # uses podman + Dockerfile (target `env`)
make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU
./scripts/build_simpoint.sh
```

To clean:

```sh
source ./setup.sh clean         # all four
source ./setup.sh clean qemu    # just QEMU build/
source ./setup.sh clean vsim
source ./setup.sh clean plugin
source ./setup.sh clean simpoint
```

### 1.5 Build the test fixtures (RISC-V ELFs)

Fixtures are small RISC-V programs that exercise specific transport
paths. They are NOT built by `setup.sh`; build them once:

```sh
make -C tests/fixtures -j
```

One fixture at a time:

```sh
make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

Output ELFs land next to the sources under
`tests/fixtures/*.elf`. The fixtures depend on the Andes
RISC-V GCC + the `libgloss_vh` semihosting library. The toolchain path
comes from `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` (see section 1.3); to override for one
invocation:

```sh
make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain
```

### 1.6 Sanity check the build

```sh
# All four artifacts present?
ls build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
ls verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
ls qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
ls tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint

# Smallest possible end-to-end - one CSR-mode handoff:
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr TIMEOUT=120 \
  bash tests/e2e.sh
```

Expected last line:

```
[rt_c_v_matmul PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)
```

If you see `skip: ... not built`, redo `source ./setup.sh` and
re-build fixtures (`make -C tests/fixtures`).

---

## 2. Configuring the simulator

There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
vars in 2.1.

### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)

`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
somewhere non-default.

| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`                 | every harness            |
| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `verilator/build/sim_*`                  | every harness            |
| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
| `SIMPOINT_BIN`  | `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`                    | SimPoint pipeline        |
| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (120 for long runs)                         | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `csr`                                            | `csr` or `pc`            |
| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` | `/dev/shm`                                       | backing dir for `--mmap-size`; redirect when /dev/shm too small |

Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:

```sh
VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
  ./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode csr
```

### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML

`verilator/config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The
default is `ax45mpv_premium`:

```yaml
cpus:
  ax45mpv_premium:
    cpu_series: 45
    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
```

Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML:

```sh
cd verilator
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml
cmake --build build -j
```

`-DVSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID=ON` registers the e2e fixtures with CTest;
`-DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON` skips Verilator (use a prebuilt model).

### 2.3 QEMU plugin args

The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:

| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | PC mode: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the CSR-insn matcher.         |
| `icount=N`           | icount mode: drain on the N-th retired insn (per vcpu).                |
| `bbv_out=PATH`       | SimPoint: emit one BBV row per `slice=N` insns into PATH.              |
| `slice=N`            | Insns per slice (used by the SimPoint stages). Must be > 0.            |
| `slice_at=K`         | SimPoint slice stage: drain at the end of the K-th slice (needs `slice=N`). |
| `drain_at_exit=1`    | Drain when QEMU exits naturally; overrides `minstret` with a plugin-side per-insn counter. Used by `./hsim run --mode simpoint` (and `./hsim estimate`) to read true `N_total`. |

If no mode arg is given, the default is CSR-insn match (CSR mode): the
plugin matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire.

Example invocation (CSR mode, just the minimal arg):

```
-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
```

Example (icount mode):

```
-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin,icount=10000
```

### 2.4 vsim CLI flags

`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:

| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | PC mode exit: drain when this PC retires.               |
| `--hybrid-icount N`           | icount mode exit: drain after N committed insns (vsim).  |
| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (e.g. OpenOCD).              |
| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |

Defaults for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the QEMU `virt` /
`andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.

Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
license-gated and off by default).

### 2.5 Requesting more memory (`--mmap-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)

By default every `./hsim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:

| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| `--mmap-size SPEC` | flag on `run`, `profile`, `archive`, `estimate` | request a larger mmap (`SPEC` = `128M`, `8G`, `1.5G`, `2T`, or raw bytes). Default `128M`. |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | override the backing directory (default `/dev/shm`). |

Selection rule is deliberately simple: if `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` is set we
use it, otherwise `/dev/shm`. We check free space via `statvfs` and
error rc=2 with a clear hint if the pinned dir can't hold the request.
There is **no fallback chain** -- we never silently switch directories
on you.

Examples:

```sh
# Small request; default backend is /dev/shm.
./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr --mmap-size 256M

# 8 GiB request that won't fit /dev/shm: redirect to a disk-backed dir.
HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch/hsim \
  ./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode icount --mmap-size 8G

# Each allocation prints one status line:
#   [hsim mmap] 8.0 GiB at /scratch/hsim (free: 64.0 GiB)
```

If your `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch default), pointing
`HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` is fine **only** if `/tmp` has enough free bytes;
otherwise pick a directory on a non-tmpfs filesystem (`/var/tmp`,
`$HOME/.cache/hsim`, `/scratch`, etc.).

The hardcoded `mktemp -p /dev/shm` paths in the shell harnesses
(`tests/e2e.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) all use
128 MiB and are unaffected.

### 2.6 Orchestrator plan YAML (used by SimPoint archive/replay)

For checkpoint workflows you describe a multi-step plan in YAML and
hand it to the orchestrator:

```yaml
session:
  mem_size: 134217728            # 128 MB shared mmap
  mmap_path: null                # null -> mktemp in /dev/shm
  elf: tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

steps:
  - model: qemu
    trigger: { kind: csr }       # CSR trigger; can also be { kind: pc, enter: 0x... } or { kind: icount, n: 5000 }
    on_exit: { archive_as: "snap/0" }
```

Run it:

```sh
python3 -m orchestrator.main run plan.yaml \
  --project-root . --workdir /tmp/run --archive-root /tmp/archives
```

Replay:

```sh
python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint /tmp/archives/snap/0 \
  --resume-with vsim --project-root . --workdir /tmp/replay
```

## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use

| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| CSR      | a kernel          | `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |
| PC       | a kernel          | PC equals a boundary: any symbol or `0x` address (both `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` required) | kernel cycles |
| icount   | a sampled window  | N retired insns (single boundary; no markers)            | window cycles          |
| SimPoint | the whole program | clustering picks representative slices, each measured like icount | whole-program estimate |

CSR/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose; icount/SimPoint sample the whole
program by instruction count (SimPoint is icount repeated, weight-combined).
How each is driven: every mode goes through `./hsim run --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint`
(simpoint is also exposed as `./hsim estimate`). The cycle figure is always
the vsim `mcycle` delta (offset 624); SimPoint extrapolates many deltas
into `estimated_cycles`.

Decision flow:

```
Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
  binary is yours to edit          -> CSR  (csrwi 0x7C0,0/1 around the kernel)
  not editable, symbol/PC at ends  -> PC   (./hsim run --mode pc
                                            --pc-start S --pc-end E)
Profiling the WHOLE program (or a CSR-less blob)?
  one window by instruction count  -> icount
  representative phases, combined  -> SimPoint  (./hsim run --mode simpoint)
```

> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (CSR/PC modes):** keep the measured
> kernel anchored inside the `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` span -- read its inputs and
> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.

## 4. Walk-through: one handoff in each mode

Each section is copy-pastable. They all share the same setup.

### 4.0 Common setup (do once per shell)

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
source ./setup.sh                         # builds + exports env vars
make -C tests/fixtures -j        # builds .elf fixtures
```

Quick env check:

```sh
echo "$VSIM_QEMU"
echo "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
echo "$VSIM_BIN"
ls tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
